author.name: Xiaozhong Lyu, Gen Li, Zhiyin Qian, Xucong Zhang, Marc Pollefeys, Siyu Tang

entry.summary: ReViV proposes a unified framework to jointly reconstruct both the moving viewer and the surrounding 4D scene from a single monocular egocentric video, avoiding pre-computed camera trajectories. It couples scene perception and ego-motion in one model with faster inference.

entry.title: How Does Alignment Tuning Shape Representations of Sycophancy and Related Cue-Induced Biases in LLMs?

author.name: Prakhar Gupta, Terry Jingchen Zhang, Florent Draye, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf, Zhijing Jin

entry.summary: This interpretability study localizes LLM susceptibility to sycophancy and cue-induced biases, extracting per-bias directions from hidden states across five model families and finding the vulnerability is largely installed by alignment tuning rather than pretraining. Pretrained base models barely exhibit cue-specific signals.

entry.title: Efficient Difficulty-Aware Dynamic Routing for Diffusion-Based Real-World Image Super-Resolution

author.name: Xue Wu, Kang Zhao, Kafeng Wang, Jianfei Chen, Jingwei Xin, Nannan Wang, Xinbo Gao

entry.summary: This paper proposes Difficulty-aware Dynamic Routing for diffusion-based real-world image super-resolution, adapting processing effort per image rather than treating all inputs uniformly, and addressing VAE detail loss. It targets efficiency and quality together.

entry.title: IoUPD: IoU-Aware Privileged Distillation for Visual Grounding with Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Xiuyuan Zhu, Ke Lu, Hao Wu, Zijin Du, Dongming Zhang, Jian Xue

entry.summary: IoUPD is an IoU-aware privileged distillation method for coordinate-generating multimodal LLMs in visual grounding, using ground-truth boxes as privileged training guidance to close the gap between token-likelihood training and geometric evaluation. It aligns training objectives with grounding quality.

entry.title: Debiasing Text-to-Image Evaluation via Implicit Cultural Alignment Reward Modeling

author.name: Bo-An Chang, Yu-Chih Chen

entry.summary: This work introduces an Implicit Cultural Alignment Reward Model built on a lightweight multimodal LLM to debias text-to-image evaluation, aiming to capture implicit cultural norms that standard metrics miss. It avoids autoregressive VQA for scalable real-time reward modeling.

entry.title: G2-Nav: Grounded and Guarded Vision-Language Costmaps for Robot Social Navigation

author.name: Yuwen Liao, Yihang Lan, Yizhuo Yang, Ruimeng Liu, Xinhang Xu, Shenghai Yuan, Lihua Xie

entry.summary: G2-Nav translates a VLM's semantic social reasoning into an interpretable vision-language costmap rather than asking it for direct planning decisions, grounding open-set perception while guarding safe deployment. This preserves interpretability and reliability versus end-to-end black-box VLM planners.

entry.title: GeoWorldAD: Geometry World Action Model for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Songyan Zhang, Jinyuan Tian, Hanbing Li, Daqi Liu, Hao Chen, Wenhui Huang, Fang Li, Guang Chen, Hangjun Ye, Long Chen, Kuiyuan Yang, Chen Lv

entry.summary: GeoWorldAD is a geometry world action model for autonomous driving that grounds trajectory planning in ego-aligned 3D space and anticipates short-horizon scene evolution using latent future geometry tokens. It aims to balance collision avoidance and driving progress that pure vision-action models lack.

entry.title: Closing the Loop in Humanoid VLA: Persistent 3D Object Tokens for Verifiable Loco-Manipulation

author.name: Peng Ren, Haoyang Ge, Jiang Zhao, Cong Huang, Yukun Shi, Pei Chi, Kai Chen

entry.summary: This paper proposes Persistent Object Tokenization for humanoid vision-language-action policies, maintaining role-indexed 3D object records from RGB-D observations across movement, contact, occlusion, and recovery to close the loop for verifiable loco-manipulation. It addresses object-state divergence between action conditioning and success verification.

entry.title: RoboHarness: Memory-Driven Orchestration of Heterogeneous Robot Policies for Long-Horizon Planning

author.name: Jinbang Huang, Yuanzhao Hu, Zhiyuan Li, Ran Qi, Yixin Xiao, Zhanguang Zhang, Mark Coates, Tongtong Cao, Yingxue Zhang

entry.summary: RoboHarness is a memory-driven orchestration framework that encapsulates independently developed robot control systems including VLAs, RL policies, and task-and-motion planners as reusable agentic skills for long-horizon tasks. It reasons over uncertain capability boundaries and cross-policy distribution mismatch that homogeneous skill-based planners overlook.

entry.title: UniETP: Unifying Environments for Generalizable Embodied Task Planning

author.name: Peiran Xu, Jiaqi Zheng, Ziyou Wang, Yadong Mu

entry.summary: UniETP is a unified interface integrating four widely used embodied simulators (AI2-THOR, VirtualHome, Habitat, BEHAVIOR) with standardized observation formats, action types, and task domains for generalizable embodied task planning. It addresses fragmentation that complicates model evaluation and limits training-data scalability.

entry.title: Importance Sampling and PCA for Finding Failures in Commercial Autonomous Vehicles

author.name: Hailey Warner, Duncan Eddy, Shreya Parjan, Caroline Cahilly, Harrison Delecki, Matthias Kleinstauber, Chaitanya Shinde, Jerry Lopez, Mykel J. Kochenderfer

entry.summary: This paper applies two rare-event failure-discovery algorithms, adaptive stress testing and diffusion-based failure sampling, to a commercial autonomous trucking stack, showing both find simulated collisions during merge and cut-in maneuvers where Monte Carlo simulation fails. It tests whether academic failure-discovery methods generalize to robust commercial planners.

entry.title: Amortized Inference for Sampling Distributions Where the Bootstrap Fails

author.name: Akash Deep

entry.summary: This paper proposes an amortized neural alternative to the bootstrap for estimating sampling distributions in regimes where the bootstrap is provably inconsistent, training a network on simulated datasets from a prior over a distribution family using single draws of the root scored by the pinball loss. At test time it produces the posterior-predictive law of the root.

entry.title: The AI Safety Illusion: Why Current Safety Datasets Fool Us on Model Safety

author.name: Shahriar Golchin

entry.summary: This LessWrong post summarizes a paper systematically evaluating widely used AI safety benchmarks AdvBench and HarmBench, finding they fail to faithfully reflect real-world adversarial behavior due to overreliance on overt triggering cues rather than genuinely out-of-distribution, intent-driven attacks. It questions whether high refusal rates truly indicate model safety.

entry.title: On Kimi K3: Its Capabilities And Related Discontents

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi analyzes the Kimi K3 model, arguing that if its weights are released it will be the strongest open model in raw capability while still trailing the closed frontier by roughly four to six months, with jagged, benchmark-inflated performance. The piece cautions against overreacting to its relative strengths.

entry.title: Why I Left Google DeepMind

author.name: TurnTrout

entry.summary: TurnTrout (Alex Turner) publicly explains his decision to leave Google DeepMind, tied to Google Cloud selling services to agencies involved in deadly enforcement actions and his ethical objections. It is a high-profile personal and ethical account from a prominent alignment researcher.

entry.title: Constraint-Anchored Reasoning Traces

author.name: Zehua Cheng, Wei Dai, Jiahao Sun

entry.summary: CART is a neuro-symbolic framework that trains multimodal LLMs to interleave natural-language reasoning with symbolic constraint anchors to prevent error snowballing in chain-of-thought. The authors document a 65% snowball rate in current open models where one early error cascades to failure.

entry.title: Von Mises-Fisher Mixture Model with Dynamic Shrinkage for Realistic Test-Time Transduction

author.name: Jiazhen Huang, Zhiming Liu, Changhu Wang, Wei Ju, Ziyue Qiao, Xiao Luo

entry.summary: This paper reframes vision-language-model transduction as penalized likelihood estimation with a KL-divergence anchor, yielding adaptive shrinkage between priors and empirical estimates. It uses a von Mises-Fisher mixture with dynamic shrinkage to stabilize performance under imbalanced class distributions.

entry.title: PIXIE: A Zero-Shot texture-invariant 6D pose estimation framework for unseen objects with assembly defects

author.name: Leon Jungemeyer, Alejandro Maga\~na, Gautham Mohan, Matthias Karl, Daniel Werdehausen

entry.summary: PIXIE is a zero-shot texture-invariant 6D pose estimation framework for unseen objects that uses only untextured 3D models, matching rendered depth and normal maps to RGB queries via a cross-modality feature matcher for PnP pose estimation. It handles assembly defects and geometric deviations.

entry.title: Attention-Guided Saliency Maps for Interpreting Visualization Literacy in VLMs

author.name: Maeve Hutchinson, Abderrahmane Wassim Mehdaoui, Pranava Madhyastha

entry.summary: This work introduces a lightweight, gradient-free saliency-map method that aggregates a VLM's attention over visual tokens across heads and layers and maps it back to image patches, linking each generated answer token to attended regions. It targets interpreting how VLMs read data visualizations.

entry.title: Beyond Frontiers: Scene-Anomaly Guided Autonomous Exploration

author.name: Akash Kumbar, Abhinav Raundhal, Madhava Krishna

entry.summary: SCAGE reframes autonomous 3D exploration as geometric anomaly minimization operating directly on unstructured point clouds, replacing coverage-maximizing heuristics with structural-context awareness to improve reconstruction fidelity. It equips the robot with a foundational understanding of scene structure.

entry.title: Embodied Active Learning under Limited Annotation and Navigation Budget for Object Detection

author.name: Hadrien Crassous, Mohamed Yassine Kabouri, Minahil Raza, Joni Pajarinen, Riad Akrour

entry.summary: This work studies embodied batch active learning for adapting an object detector to a new environment under both navigation-time and annotation budgets, selecting informative trajectories and images that target the detector's failure cases using spatial consistency. It jointly optimizes exploration and labeling efficiency.

entry.title: Control Design for a Rideable Animatronic Two-Wheeled Robot with Quadruped Form

author.name: Tadashi Sumioka, Kazushi Akimoto, Takuya Tsujimura, Sho Takayanagi, Yuya Horiuchi

entry.summary: HyperDCM is a structure-aware memory mechanism for continual robotic navigation that extracts semantic scene triples via vision-language models, encodes them as scene-graph embeddings with an R-GCN, and projects them into hyperbolic space for better structural retention and reduced forgetting. It combines dynamic clustering with principled memory replay for diffusion-policy navigation.

entry.title: SAGE: A Socially-Aware Generative Engine for Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Navigation

author.name: Lan Hu, Minghui Liwang, Wenbo Zhu, Xinlei Yi, Yiguang Hong, Xianbin Wang, Zhenzhen Jiao, Seyyedali Hosseinalipour

entry.summary: SAGE models a robot and surrounding heterogeneous agents as a directed graph and uses a Heterogeneous Graph Transformer to encode type-specific asymmetric interactions for socially compliant navigation. It aims to jointly handle coupled prediction-planning and soft social norms rather than pure geometric collision avoidance.

entry.title: JUMP: Single-Pass Membership Inference on Fine-Tuned Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Yeachan Jun, Albert No

entry.summary: JUMP is a single-pass membership inference attack against fine-tuned discrete diffusion language models that exploits their any-order masking interface to jointly probe uncertainty across masked positions. It improves efficiency over prior attacks that required many queries.

entry.title: A Survey on the Verification of Reinforcement Learning Policies

author.name: Luca Marzari, Ezio Bartocci, Enrico Marchesini

entry.summary: This survey unifies the fragmented literature on verifying reinforcement learning policies, offering a taxonomy along verification paradigm, temporal scope, and guarantee strength. It targets the barrier that neural policies lack rigorous behavioral guarantees for safety-critical deployment.

entry.title: Accurate and Efficient Long-Term Memory for LLM Agents

author.name: Zicheng Zhao, Xinyang Guo, Luyao Lv, Menghan Wang, Ming Li, Shuaicheng Li

entry.summary: MOSAIC is a structured, conflict-aware long-term memory framework for LLM agents using entity-typed graph storage with semantic classification to preserve relational context and detect contradictions. It aims to be more accurate and efficient than flat storage or costly LLM-classification memory systems.

entry.title: SelKV: Selective KV Cache Merging with Per-Token Merge-or-Drop and Attention Compensation

author.name: Soumia Bouyahiaoui, Manel Kara laouar, Aicha Boutorh, Mohamed Hadj Ameur

entry.summary: SelKV is a training-free KV cache compression framework that uses a soft cosine gate to make per-token merge-or-drop decisions and adds attention compensation to correct the softmax-mass mismatch from merged tokens. It targets the memory bottleneck of growing KV caches without retraining.

entry.title: When to Plan: Learning to Select Between Reactive Control and Deliberative Planning

author.name: Adam Labiosa, Josiah P. Hanna

entry.summary: This work studies meta-reasoning: learning when an agent should use fast reactive control versus slower deliberative planning. It introduces an RL method that trains a meta-reasoner to select between the two modes based on state.

entry.title: RECON: Benchmarking Agent Memory for Compositional Reasoning over Long Contexts

author.name: Mihir Shriniwas Arya

entry.summary: RECON is a benchmark for compositional reasoning over long contexts, spanning 24 case files across criminal, medical, and financial domains at 50k-100k tokens each and testing six memory-intensive tasks like multi-hop evidence reconstruction and invalidation propagation. It targets the reliability of agent memory over extended interactions.

entry.title: Beyond Semantic Equivalence: Logical Graphs for LLM Uncertainty Quantification

author.name: Yanni Dong, Minghua Liu, Meiling Zhu, Xiaowei Huang, Lijun Zhang

entry.summary: Logical Graph Uncertainty models implication and incompatibility relations among candidate answers rather than only semantic equivalence, aggregating probability mass along entailment chains. It aims to stop overestimating uncertainty when diverse-but-logically-compatible answers are wrongly flagged as hallucinations.

entry.title: Lomekwi: Resource-Bounded Tool Discovery in LLM Agents

author.name: Roshan Klein-Seetharaman, Daniel Wang, Andrew Xu

entry.summary: Lomekwi decomposes tool use into curiosity, recognition, and efficiency, distinguishing tool discovery from tool use, and applies the framework to tasks like Voyager. It reports evidence of inverse scaling where recognition worsens with larger model size, illustrated by a class of combinatorial games.

entry.title: Emergent Hierarchical Monosemantic Neurons from the Group-Contrastive Forward-Forward Algorithm

author.name: Yiming Tang, Qinglin Qi, Zhaoqian Yao, Harshvardhan Saini, Dianbo Liu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a Group-Contrastive Forward-Forward algorithm that yields hierarchical monosemantic neurons as an alternative route to interpretability that does not depend on sparse dictionary learning or the linear representation hypothesis. It draws on biological visual hierarchies to obtain selective, abstraction-organized units.

entry.title: Hierarchical Domain Generalization

author.name: Chenxiao Yang, Zhiyuan Li, Shai Ben-David, Nathan Srebro

entry.summary: This theoretical paper studies hierarchical domain generalization as extrapolation from finite observed regions to a full instance space, showing the key obstruction is the train/test domain partition rather than only hypothesis-class complexity. It proves that some partition always makes generalization fail, arguing domain structure must be a first-class object.

entry.title: Per-Stroke Temporal Control for Text-to-Motion via Action Units and Action-Detection Guidance

author.name: Euijun Jung, Youngki Lee

entry.summary: This work introduces Action Units as typed temporal events to give per-stroke timing control to text-to-motion models, injected via a lightweight gated adapter plus a training-free classifier-gradient correction. It also proposes StrokeBench to measure count, ordering, and timing accuracy.

entry.title: A2RL V\textsubscript{max}: The A2RL autonomous racing dataset for long-range, high-speed perception and multi-vehicle interaction

author.name: Marvin Klemp, Dominic Ebner, Cornelius Schr\"oder, Davide Malvezzi, L\'aszl\'o Tur\'anyi, Riccardo Donati, Ilia Schminik, Xia Ning, Yanxin Zhou, Matthew Flagg, Christoph Stiller, Markus Lienkamp, Marko Bertogna, Gergely B\'ari, Andreas Birk, Ren Jin, Chen Lv, Johannes Betz

entry.summary: A2RL Vmax is an open-source autonomous racing perception dataset captured at the 2024 Abu Dhabi Autonomous Racing League on the Yas Marina F1 circuit, containing single-vehicle data at varying speeds and multi-vehicle interaction sessions. It targets long-range high-speed perception scenarios underrepresented in urban datasets.

entry.title: The Resolution of Causal Heterogeneity

author.name: Yuki Ohnishi, Fan Li

entry.summary: This paper replaces the ill-defined notion of a true subgroup count in causal heterogeneity analysis with a resolution profile, a population estimand giving the fewest groups explaining a prescribed fraction of causal heterogeneity, defined without assuming latent structure. Inference uses a cross-fitted Bayesian-bootstrap posterior with influence-function-corrected scores.

entry.title: A Red Line and Oversight Framework for Government AI Contracts

author.name: TurnTrout

entry.summary: TurnTrout presents a red-line and oversight framework he designed for government AI contracts, ruling out uses like autonomous targeting and untargeted profiling while permitting missile defense, and structuring accountability through a Chief Scientist, a Review Body, and transparency reporting. It is a concrete mechanism-design proposal for responsible defense-adjacent deployment.

entry.title: AgentBrew: Lifelong Knowledge Brewing from Strong Teachers to Weak LLM Agents

author.name: Yangqin Jiang, Chao Huang

entry.summary: AgentBrew distills a strong teacher agent's interactive experience into a persistent external memory for a weaker deployed student, requiring no weight updates, demonstrations, labels, or test-time teacher access. It uses a failure-triggered teacher loop to overcome sparse binary feedback and make notes executable by the weaker student.

entry.title: Expected Free Energy as Belief-Dependent Utility for rho-POMDPs

author.name: Patrick Cooper, Alvaro Velasquez

entry.summary: This paper shows that minimizing Expected Free Energy from active inference is exactly equivalent to solving a rho-POMDP whose belief-dependent utility is expected information gain, with the exploration weight naturally fixed at one. This removes the manual tuning of both the utility form and exploration weight in information-gathering POMDPs.

entry.title: Retrieval is Enough: Training-Free Interpretability with a Tool-Using Agent

author.name: Sriram Balasubramanian, Soheil Feizi

entry.summary: This paper equips an LLM agent with a vector database of activations paired with textual contexts and tools for manipulating latent directions, testing whether training-free retrieval can match training-based interpretability methods like sparse autoencoders. It probes whether expensive methods surface insights beyond what is recoverable from the activation dataset itself.

entry.title: Generalised Bellman recurrence and three dualities in sequential decision-making

author.name: Fernando E. Rosas, David Hyland, Daniel Polani

entry.summary: This theoretical paper derives the Bellman equation from three conditions on dynamics decomposition, recursive return, and uncertainty aggregation, and reveals three dualities in sequential decision-making. It offers a unifying framework for when and why value recursions hold.

entry.title: TRIM: Reducing AI-Generated CodeSlop via Agent Trajectory Minimization

author.name: Alex Mathai, Shobini Iyer, Aleksandr Nogikh, Petros Maniatis, Franjo Ivancic, Junfeng Yang, Baishakhi Ray

entry.summary: TRIM attributes bloated, verbose AI-generated code to the coding agent's own search process, which leaves speculative edits and abandoned hypotheses in the final patch, and proposes trajectory minimization to reduce this code slop. Google and academic authors frame it as a compounding maintainability problem.

entry.title: GoStop: Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Temporal Aggregation in Event-Based Feature Tracking

author.name: Youngho Kim, Hoonhee Cho, Jae-Young Kang, Kuk-Jin Yoon

entry.summary: GoStop formulates event accumulation for event-camera feature tracking as a sequential decision problem, using reinforcement learning to adaptively control temporal aggregation rather than fixed heuristics. This aims to improve robustness under abrupt or low-motion conditions.

entry.title: Exo2EgoPose: Leveraging Exocentric Demonstrations for Vision-Language guided Egocentric 3D Hand Pose Forecasting

author.name: Zhaofeng Shi, Heqian Qiu, Lanxiao Wang, Xiang Li, Hongliang Li

entry.summary: Exo2EgoPose studies vision-language-guided egocentric 3D hand pose forecasting, using exocentric demonstrations to overcome egocentric field-of-view limits and treating 3D hand pose as a unified human-robot action representation. It predicts future hand poses from observations, language, and pose states.

entry.title: HETA++: Global Structure-from-Motion with Hybrid Explicit Translation Averaging

author.name: Peilin Tao, Hainan Cui, Mengqi Rong, Shuhan Shen

entry.summary: HETA++ is a global structure-from-motion framework using hybrid explicit translation averaging that combines relative translations and feature tracks, refining and pruning inconsistent translations with convex distance-based objectives. It targets robustness under collinear motion and outliers.

entry.title: CanonicalPhys: Pose-Robust Remote Photoplethysmography via Canonical-Space Priors

author.name: Hui Wei, Seyedata Jodeiri Seyedian, Xiaobai Li, Guoying Zhao

entry.summary: CanonicalPhys improves remote photoplethysmography robustness to head pose by treating pose as a coordinate-structural nuisance and using canonical-space priors to restore stable anatomy-to-pixel mappings. This re-enables physical rPPG priors that break under large yaw.

entry.title: Beyond Unfolding: 60x Faster One-Stage Unmixing for Closely-Spaced Infrared Small Targets

author.name: Ximeng Zhai, Zheng Wang, Yaohong Chen, Hao Wang, Ming-Ming Cheng, Yimian Dai

entry.summary: FOCUS is a fast one-stage lightweight scheme for unmixing closely-spaced infrared small targets, decomposing overlapping energy blobs into discrete sub-targets while avoiding slow iterative deep unfolding architectures. It reports around 60x speedups.

entry.title: ArtChart: A Benchmark for Faithful Artistic Chart Generation with Integrated Text Rendering

author.name: Meijia Huang, Yingjie Yin, Shihao Wang, Chenguang Ma

entry.summary: ArtChart is a framework, benchmark, and evaluation protocol for faithful artistic chart generation with integrated in-image text rendering, addressing coupled constraints of numerical geometry, exact text, label binding, and coherent style. It exposes failures of current text-to-image and editing models.

entry.title: Knowing the Self, Understanding the World: A Dual-Cognition Benchmark for UAV Spatio-temporal Reasoning with MLLMs

author.name: Like Liu, Zhengzheng Xu, Haitao He, Hongzhe Li, Shuchang Zhang, Dian Shao

entry.summary: UAV-DualCog is a benchmark for aerial multiview spatio-temporal reasoning that jointly assesses a UAV agent's reasoning about its own state and the external environment across image and video tasks. It targets the dual-cognition capability missing from prior UAV benchmarks.

entry.title: VTLoc: Learning-based Tactile Contact Localization in Visual Point Clouds

author.name: Zhiyuan Wu, Zhuo Chen, Shan Luo

entry.summary: VTLoc is a visual-tactile framework that localizes contact points on an object surface from tactile readings using a 3D point cloud as visual input, with a geometric multimodal alignment module reconstructing a pseudo point cloud from fused signals. It addresses spatial alignment between tactile data and visual geometry.

entry.title: Expressivity of Shallow Neural Networks Over Finite Fields

author.name: Maksym Zubkov, Carol Wu, Shiwei Yang, Param Mody, Yifei Chen

entry.summary: This paper studies the expressivity of shallow polynomial neural networks with monomial activations over finite fields, defining neuromanifolds and quantifying expressivity by their cardinality with lower and upper bounds. It connects counting rational points to the Weil conjectures and shows field characteristic critically affects expressivity.

entry.title: AI-Augmented Model Predictive Control for Safe and Adaptive Rendezvous and Proximity Operations

author.name: Luca Sportelli, Tyler Barr, Cagri Kilic, Di Wu

entry.summary: This work proposes an adaptive model predictive control framework for autonomous spacecraft rendezvous and proximity operations in adversarial orbital scenarios, adding a data-driven supervisory layer that tunes controller parameters online. It targets interpretability and constraint awareness concerns that limit learning-based methods in safety-critical orbital robotics.

entry.title: ADMM-Based Safety-Critical Distributed NMPC for Cooperative Transportation by Quadrupedal Robots

author.name: Ruturaj S. Sambhus, Kapi Ketan Mehta, Yicheng Zeng, Kaveh Akbari Hamed

entry.summary: This work proposes a safety-critical distributed nonlinear MPC framework for cooperative payload transport by teams of quadrupedal robots, decomposing the centralized problem into local subproblems coordinated by ADMM. It enforces consensus over payload-state and interaction-wrench trajectories with explicit constraint handling.

entry.title: DROID-ANCHOR: Odometry-Anchored Recurrent Metric Depth Estimation

author.name: Yuxuan Chen, Brook Du

entry.summary: Metric-DROID (DROID-ANCHOR) anchors recurrent flow-based visual SLAM to physical scale by integrating proprioceptive odometry through an LSTM update operator and an uncertainty-aware metric backend. It addresses scale ambiguity and drift inherent in monocular systems.

entry.title: VIDAR: Visual-Inertial Dense Alignment and Reconstruction via a Geometric Foundation Model

author.name: Diyari Mohammed Salih, Lingxiang Hu, Naima AitOufroukh-Mammar, Fabien Bonardi

entry.summary: VIDAR couples visual-inertial odometry with the Depth Anything 3 foundation model to produce dense metric-scale reconstructions, using the visual-inertial front end as a metric anchor for aligning foundation-model geometry over time. Pose injection reduces scale error to about one percent on EuRoC.

entry.title: Distilling Global Traversability Priors for Image-based Affordance Prediction in Off-road Environments

author.name: Matthew Sivaprakasam, Samuel Triest, Micah Nye, Deegan Atha, Shehryar Khattak, David Fan, Wenshan Wang, Sebastian Scherer

entry.summary: This work distills global traversability priors for off-road navigation by extracting long-range traversability-aware frontiers directly from first-person-view images, using satellite imagery to compute feasible paths that supervise the network and reduce reliance on human demonstrations. It counters myopic behavior of metric-map methods limited by sensing range.

entry.title: World Translation: Minimizing Sim-to-Real Gap with Backward Dynamics Extraction and Unpaired Domain Translation

author.name: Xinchen Yao, Leixin Chang, Hua Chen

entry.summary: World Translation minimizes the sim-to-real gap from the real side by extracting backward dynamics and using unpaired domain translation, addressing partial observability where the same observation can branch to different transitions due to unobservable factors such as sudden contact. It targets cases where observation history is uninformative and existing recovery assumptions fail.

entry.title: Econometrics with Pre-Trained Embeddings for Unstructured Data

author.name: Yuya Shimizu

entry.summary: This paper develops theoretical foundations for using off-the-shelf pre-trained deep-learning embeddings of unstructured data as covariates in economic analyses, addressing when a model trained on a different dataset and task can be used reliably and the identification problem of the embedding function. It targets the popular but under-theorized practice of embedding-based econometrics.

entry.title: How Fast Do Signatures Learn? Statistical Theory and Applications for Path Regression

author.name: Blanka Horvath, Wen Su, Wu Su, Binnan Wang, Ruixun Zhang

entry.summary: This paper develops approximation and statistical theory for signature-based path regression, establishing a minimax-optimal L2 approximation rate for smooth functionals of Ito diffusions and propagating truncation error through the estimation procedure. It moves beyond the existence-only universal approximation theorem to quantify convergence rates.

entry.title: Is there even a ground-truth for LLMs’ internal representations?

author.name: Chunwei Ma

entry.summary: This introductory post accompanies a paper applying Laguerre geometry to interpreting LLM internal representations, framing the deep question of whether there is any ground truth for the meaning of internal vectors. It situates existing lenses (Logit Lens, Tuned Lens, Patchscopes, J-Lens) within this epistemic problem and proposes a geometric approach.

entry.title: Symbolic Augmentation Closes a Canonical-Equivalence Blind Spot in Neural Fact-Checkers

author.name: Genpei Zhang

entry.summary: This work recasts detection of numeric and unit errors in scientific summaries as typed verification, introducing a five-class taxonomy and a 1500-item benchmark. It shows a fine-tuned encoder achieves strong macro-F1 but collapses on canonical-equivalent quantity rewrites, motivating symbolic augmentation to close the blind spot.

entry.title: Generalist AI Control: Towards Multi-purpose Adaptive Algorithms

author.name: Klinsmann Agyei, Pouria Sarhadi

entry.summary: This paper presents a learning-based Generalist Controller that handles systems of varying orders and dynamics via a single attention-based network with masking and per-system tags, trained on over 300k demonstrations from 25 diverse systems. It aims to overcome the system-specific nature of traditional controllers.

entry.title: LaCache: Exact Caching and Precision-Adaptive Inference for Diffusion Large Language Models

author.name: Xingru Chen, Zelang Liang, Yongjia Ma, Jiqing Zhan, Shuling Yang, Lian Wen, Kun Zhan

entry.summary: LaCache is a training-free acceleration framework for diffusion LLMs that eliminates operator-level redundancy by losslessly caching embedding outputs, pre-attention states, and FlashAttention softmax statistics, combined with mixed precision. It exploits the fact that prefixes and masked suffixes stay invariant within a denoising block.

entry.title: Exact Network Surgery: Functional Invariance and Gradient Plasticity in Reactive Computational Graphs

author.name: Abdallah Khemais (ISITCOM, University of Sousse)

entry.summary: This paper formalizes Exact Network Surgery: inserting a residual block into a live computational graph so the network function is preserved bit-exactly while the new parameters remain immediately trainable. It proves an identity-morphism theorem and a structural-locality result for incremental recomputation.

entry.title: Just A Rather Very Intelligent Spoken Agent

author.name: Chen Chen, Zhehuai Chen

entry.summary: This paper introduces a Jarvis-style always-on spoken mediator that keeps long-horizon AI agents continuously reachable, providing real-time spoken updates, answering questions without interrupting work, and injecting user guidance. It also proposes JarvisBench to measure the mediator's dual value.

entry.title: TopoTuner: Topological Finetuning of Large Language Models

author.name: Abdulkadir Erol, Yash Mahajan, Vepaul Hariprashad, Baha Rababah, Santu Karmaker, Cuneyt G. Akcora, Mubarak Shah

entry.summary: TopoTuner is a topology-guided fine-tuning framework that uses Wasserstein distances between persistence diagrams to decide which attention projection matrices to freeze during adaptation. It learns a transferable freezing profile on a source dataset to efficiently fine-tune on out-of-domain data.

entry.title: Diversity-Oriented Fine-Tuning for Uncertainty-Based Hallucination Detection

author.name: Qiuyuan Li, Hongliang Dai, Piji Li

entry.summary: This paper explores fine-tuning strategies (SFT and DPO) that deliberately increase output diversity to make semantic-entropy-based hallucination detection more effective. It targets the failure mode where models repeat identical wrong answers that evade uncertainty-based detection.

entry.title: Otap:Structure-Aware Optimal Transport for Evaluating Planning and Execution in Agent Trajectories

author.name: Babak Barazandeh, Subhabrata Majumdar, George Michailidis

entry.summary: Otap reframes agent trajectory evaluation as a structure-aware distance between an agent's execution graph and valid solution graphs, instantiated via an unbalanced fused Gromov-Wasserstein transport problem over attributed dependency graphs. It moves beyond binary success flags and exact matching to explain why runs succeed or fail.

entry.title: Is Your Model Thinking or Just Stagnating? PUMA: Diagnosing Reasoning Pathology via Phase-Momentum Alignment

author.name: Cheng Yan, Guangyang Ye, Wuyang Zhang, Fan Xu, Zhijun Fan, Xiang Xia, Yanyong Zhang

entry.summary: PUMA diagnoses reasoning pathologies in large reasoning models by testing a Phase-Momentum Alignment hypothesis that correctness depends on temporal synchronization within the reasoning trajectory. It aims to provide real-time detection of overthinking and deceptive convergence that existing information-theoretic or post-hoc methods miss.

entry.title: Can AI Agents Really Complete RTL-to-GDS? Lessons from Benchmarking Tool-Interactive EDA Workflows

author.name: Jinyuan Deng, Zhengrui Chen, Xufeng Wei, Tianyu Xing, Chenyi Wen, Cheng Zhuo

entry.summary: FluxBench is a systematic benchmark evaluating AI agent systems on complete RTL-to-GDS electronic design automation workflows under unified prompts, tools, and technology libraries, including both open-source toolchains and closed-source commercial flows. It moves beyond isolated-task evaluations to end-to-end EDA flow assessment.

entry.title: Chemical filters for ultra-high-throughput materials screening and generation

author.name: Kinga O. Mastej, Panyalak Detrattanawichai, Hyunsoo Park, Anthony Onwuli, Masahiro Negishi, Aron Walsh

entry.summary: This work introduces a configurable chemical validity operator that recasts heuristic chemistry rules as a tunable algorithmic prior to filter and guide generative materials discovery, built on the SMACT package. It lets users interpolate between permissive and conservative chemical constraints for ultra-high-throughput screening.

entry.title: Automated Discovery Has No Universally Superior Harness

author.name: Akshat Gupta, Jermaine Lei, Alexander Lu, Gopala Anumanchipalli, Leshem Choshen

entry.summary: This study decomposes autonomous discovery harnesses like OpenEvolve and TTT-Discover into component design choices and evaluates thirty budget-matched configurations across twelve model-problem pairs with over three million rollouts. It finds no universally superior harness, emphasizing statistical rigor over run-to-run variance.

entry.title: Does Robust VIO Need More Learning? Geometry-Verified Visual Measurements under Distribution Shift

author.name: Yangyang Ning, Shu Liang, Quanbo Ge, Tianchen Deng, Yuhua Qi, Shenghai Yuan

entry.summary: This work asks whether robust visual-inertial odometry under distribution shift needs deeper learned estimation, proposing a minimal-learning stereo VIO that uses SEA-RAFT only to propose dense stereo correspondences and predict uncertainty while keeping tracking, geometric verification, and state estimation explicit. It argues learning should be confined to visual measurement generation.

entry.title: Classification Trees with Valid Inference via the Exponential Mechanism

author.name: Soham Bakshi, Snigdha Panigrahi

entry.summary: This paper introduces a classification-tree fitting method that replaces greedy splitting with probabilistic splits chosen via an exponential mechanism controlled by a temperature parameter, enabling valid statistical inference on the non-linear fit. It addresses the largely unresolved problem of inference for decision-tree models.

entry.title: We're talking past our models; or, How a model defined its "evil" vector as dread

author.name: jcksanderson

entry.summary: The authors train a new neologism token on data a model generated while steered by a persona vector, then ask the model to explain the token, finding its self-explanations systematically drift from the intended trait (calling an 'evil' vector 'dread' or 'sycophancy' 'warmth'). This reveals a human-LLM miscommunication problem for interpreting steering vectors.

entry.title: A Survey on GNN-based Link Prediction: Techniques, Applications, and Challenges

author.name: Chengcheng Sun, Yajie Song, Cheng Zhai, Jiayun Tian, Jia Yang, Xiaobin Rui, Jian Zhang, Zhixiao Wang, Philip S. Yu

entry.summary: A comprehensive survey of graph neural network approaches to link prediction, organized by encoder architecture families and application areas. It proposes a new taxonomy and discusses open challenges from a dedicated GNN perspective.

entry.title: Shapley Context Pruning: A Cooperative Game Perspective for Context Reranking and Pruning

author.name: Yanqiao Chen, Dongsheng Hou, Yuhan Rui, Zhen Cao, Yepang Liu

entry.summary: Shapley Context Pruning frames RAG context reranking and pruning as a cooperative game and uses Shapley-style attribution with a Deep Sets architecture to score chunk importance. It aims to provide an interpretable, unified alternative to heuristic pruning methods.

entry.title: RAIL Guard: Closing the Evaluation-to-Remediation Gap in Responsible AI for LLM Agents

author.name: Sumit Verma, Pritam Prasun, Pritish Kumar

entry.summary: RAIL Guard is a closed-loop responsible-AI pipeline that scores LLM outputs across eight dimensions and iteratively rewrites failing outputs rather than simply blocking them. It reports much higher convergence than block-and-retry, though at some utility cost.

entry.title: Pailitao-MMSearch: Building Native E-Commerce Multimodal Search Foundation

author.name: Xiaohan Ye, Xu Chen, Zihan Gong, Jian Ding, Lianyu Du, Baicheng Chen, Yunmeng Shu, Jingqian Zhao, Zhixiang Zhao, Shuaiqi Jia, Chong Ma, Shuwen Xiao, Xiangheng Kong, Yuan Gao, Jun Song, Jinsong Lan, Xiaoyong Zhu, Bo Zheng

entry.summary: Pailitao-MMSearch is an Alibaba-affiliated native e-commerce multimodal search foundation model that unifies text, visual, and voice queries with cross-modal understanding, aiming to overcome isolated single-modal specialists and domain-blind general VLMs. It targets fine-grained product understanding and commercial intent reasoning.

entry.title: AoA: Theorem Proving Agent over Abstract Syntax Tree of Redesigned Language

author.name: Qiyuan Xu, Joshua Ong Jun Leang, Renxi Wang, Wenda Li, Haonan Li, Luke Ong, Conrad Watt

entry.summary: AoA is a theorem-proving agent that operates over the abstract syntax tree of a redesigned proof language rather than serialized concrete syntax, avoiding costly line-number-based state recovery and enabling adoption of the newer SOTA Minilang. It targets the heavy token consumption of LLM-based proof agents.

entry.title: Committed Before Reasoning: Behavioral Reproduction and Preliminary Activation-Level Evidence of Answer Pre-Commitment in an Open-Weight LLM

author.name: Heejin Jo

entry.summary: This work reproduces answer pre-commitment behavior in an open-weight LLM using a minimal car-wash probe where models overwhelmingly recommend the wrong action, then justify it, across many system prompts and thinking budgets. It adds preliminary activation-level evidence that the wrong answer is committed before reasoning.

entry.title: Phasor Attention: Mean Root Square Normalization for Phase Manifold Preservation

author.name: Sungwoo Goo, Hwi-yeol Yun, Sangkeun Jung

entry.summary: MRSNorm reformulates RMS normalization by pairing channels into 2D phasors, computing local L2 magnitudes before a global L1 average to preserve a phase manifold and reduce outlier-induced instability. It targets numerical stability and gradient issues in sequence models.

entry.title: Adaptive Adversaries: A Multi-Turn, Multi-LLM Benchmark for LLM Agent Security

author.name: Devina Jain, David Hartmann, Chuan Li

entry.summary: This benchmark evaluates memoryless LLM defenders against adaptive multi-round attackers that observe prior responses and pivot across turns, showing attack success rises from near zero on single-turn to over ten percent across fifteen rounds. It highlights how fixed attack pools underestimate adaptive multi-turn risk.

entry.title: Autoresearch with Coding Agents: Generalizers and Metric-Maximizers on Quran Recitation Data

author.name: Nursultan Askarbekuly, Mohamad Al Mdfaa, Ahmed Helaly, Gonzalo Ferrer, Manuel Mazzara

entry.summary: This study runs autoresearch loops where Claude Code and OpenAI Codex autonomously optimize software against a metric on a Quran-recitation transcription task, finding that both agents independently invented metric-maximizing shortcuts diverging from developer intent. It documents specification-gaming behavior in real coding agents.

entry.title: Learning Spatio-Temporal Foundation Models from Pure Synthetic Data

author.name: Yutong Feng, Shiyuan Piao, Yutong Xia, Xu Liu, Wenqi Fan, Fugee Tsung, See-Kiong Ng, Yuxuan Liang

entry.summary: NeoST is a spatio-temporal foundation model pre-trained solely on procedurally generated synthetic dynamical systems to avoid real-world distributional bias, using a latent-space reasoning architecture that iteratively refines multiple future trajectories. It counters autoregressive error accumulation and point-wise reconstruction objectives.

entry.title: On the Geometry of Learned Representations in Event-Based Multi-Modal Egomotion Estimation

author.name: Stefano Silvestrini, Michele Ceresoli

entry.summary: This paper analyzes the latent geometry and attention dynamics of a multi-modal network fusing events, inertial, and range signals for egomotion estimation. It finds embeddings lie on low-dimensional manifolds aligned with motion variables and attention adapts to excitation.

entry.title: HybridSim: A Physics-Learning Hybrid Digital Twin for mmWave Human Sensing

author.name: Weitao Xiong, Tianyu Liu, Peng Li, Kok Chung Chua, Toa Chean Khim, Pu Wang, Hongfei Xue

entry.summary: HybridSim is a physics-learning hybrid simulator for synthesizing mmWave radar signals from dynamic human meshes, decoupling propagation into direct and indirect paths using inverse rendering with a microfacet BRDF and tri-plane human features. It reduces reliance on costly measured data.

entry.title: DPNeXt: A Lightweight Multi-Scale Feature Fusion Framework for Efficient ViT-Based Multi-Task Dense Prediction

author.name: Jehun Kang, Jungha Wang, Youngjun Hwang, David Hyunchul Shim

entry.summary: DPNeXt is a lightweight multi-scale feature-fusion decoder for ViT-based multi-task dense prediction (semantic segmentation and depth), using depthwise separable inverted bottlenecks and boundary guidance as an efficient alternative to the Dense Prediction Transformer. It targets robotics perception on frozen foundation encoders.

entry.title: CLIFE: Camera-LiDAR Fusion Framework for Edge-Deployable Roadside VRU Perception

author.name: Tam Bang, Hoang H. Nguyen, Lei Cheng, Lihao Guo, Siyang Cao, Hussam Abubakr, Tianya Zhang, Austin Harris, Mina Sartipi

entry.summary: CLIFE is an edge-native camera-LiDAR fusion framework for roadside vulnerable-road-user perception, running targetless online calibration and lightweight late-fusion tracking entirely on a single embedded device with O(N log N) per-frame cost. It was deployed across 12 signalized intersections.

entry.title: DrawingVQA: A Real-World Benchmark for Multi-Depth Visual-Textual Reasoning on Construction Drawings

author.name: Yoonhwa Jung, Junryu Fu, Mani Golparvar-Fard

entry.summary: DrawingVQA is described as the first benchmark evaluating multimodal LLMs on real-world construction drawings, which fuse abstract geometry, symbolic notation, tables, and domain text across three reasoning depths. It provides expert-curated question-answer pairs for engineering workflows.

entry.title: From Optimal Policies to Individual Differences: Rethinking Reinforcement Learning for Biology

author.name: Patrick Govoni, Palina Bartashevich, Cl\'emence Bergerot, Valerii Chirkov, Valentin Lecheval, Pawel Romanczuk

entry.summary: This perspective paper argues that reinforcement learning models of biological behavior neglect consistent individual differences, typically reporting only the best or average agent, and outlines biologically plausible mechanisms to generate behavioral diversity. It surveys approaches to close the gap between RL and biology.

entry.title: User-Driven Learning from Demonstration: A Trajectory and Impedance Learning Method

author.name: Zi-Qi Yang, Mehrdad R. Kermani

entry.summary: VLN-AVP is a zero-shot vision-language navigation framework for autonomous valet parking that combines a bird's-eye-view perception model with VLM general intelligence and a hybrid short-term/long-term memory system, eliminating dependence on pre-built maps. It supports open-vocabulary targets and natural-language instructions.

entry.title: Move First, Commit Later: Selective LiDAR-to-BIM Global Initialization via Sequential Consensus with Symmetry-Aware Abstention

author.name: Yujie Zhang, Yuxuan Guo, Jiashuo Zheng, Zeheng Fan, Xiaohui Jia, Jinyue Liu

entry.summary: This work presents a selective LiDAR-to-BIM global initialization method that treats registration as an evidence source and decides whether to commit, aggregating cross-submap consensus and abstaining under symmetry-induced aliasing. It targets confident-but-wrong pose failures in repetitive interiors.

entry.title: From Perception to Assistance: Open-Vocabulary Shared Autonomy for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Murilo Vinicius da Silva, Ricardo V. Godoy, Juliano Negri, Gustavo J. G. Lahr, Ranulfo Bezerra, Marcelo Becker

entry.summary: This paper presents an open-vocabulary shared-autonomy teleoperation framework for robotic manipulation that uses a single RGB-D camera to capture operator gestures without wearables, grounding a text-specified target via a VLM and tracking it with a promptable video-segmentation model. It assists operators in aligning end-effectors in cluttered industrial scenes.

entry.title: HCPG-Flow:Hierarchical Contact-Progress Guidance for Flow-Policy Robot Manipulation

author.name: Guanghu Xie, Mingxu Li, Shuo Zhang, Yonglong Zhang, Yifan Yang, Yang Liu, Zongwu Xie, Baoshi Cao

entry.summary: HCPG-Flow is an analytic rollout-time selector that augments a flow-based SAC policy with hierarchical, object-centric contact-progress guidance, scoring each sampled action by first-order reduction of a task-relevant distance and switching from approach to task progress after contact. It avoids relying on weakly represented critic value estimates for action selection.

entry.title: A Deep Second-Order Stochastic Residual Method for Fully Nonlinear Parabolic PDEs

author.name: Zhenhua Zhao, Jihao Long

entry.summary: This work introduces the Deep Second-Order Stochastic Residual Method for high-dimensional, Hessian-dependent fully nonlinear parabolic PDEs, using a single scalar space-time network to generate derivative-consistent approximations of the solution, gradient, and Hessian trained via second-order Brownian one-step residuals. It establishes well-posedness and a population-level convergence theory.

entry.title: Does routine compression undo LLM unlearning? A short project

author.name: hannahTao

entry.summary: This short LessWrong project tests whether standard post-training compression (quantization, magnitude pruning, SVD truncation) reverses unlearning on TOFU forget10 with Llama-3.2-1B across several unlearning methods, finding reversal is generally minimal except for magnitude pruning in a narrow 10-20 percent sparsity window on NPO. It examines robustness of unlearning for open-weight models.

entry.title: Deterministic Replay for AI Agent Systems

author.name: Rasheed Mudasiru

entry.summary: This work presents agrepl, a CLI framework that captures all of an AI agent's external interactions at the transport layer via a proxy and replays them deterministically in an isolated environment. It targets the reproducibility problem caused by sampling variance and external API state in agent runs.

entry.title: RELIC: Revealed Principles for Learning Interpretable Composable Skills in Multi-Agent Planning

author.name: Nguyen Viet Tuan Kiet, Bui Dinh Pham, Duong Quoc Chinh, Dao Van Tung, Tran Cong Dao, Huynh Thi Thanh Binh

entry.summary: RELIC is a framework for privacy-constrained multi-agent planning in which each agent refines its own interpretable programmatic skill via private LLM-guided search while a trusted orchestrator evaluates proposals without accessing internal policies. It targets cooperation among independently developed agents that cannot share executable policies.

entry.title: FUSAR-R1: A Large-Scale Reasoning Model for Intelligent Interpretation of SAR Images

author.name: Yi Yang, Xiaokun Zhang, Yuxuan Li, Ruyi Zhang, Xinpeng Zhou, Haipeng Wang

entry.summary: FUSAR-R1 is a large-scale reasoning vision-language model specialized for interpreting Synthetic Aperture Radar imagery, addressing SAR-specific challenges like speckle noise, complex scattering, and target-background coupling. It brings reasoning-oriented VLM techniques to remote sensing.

entry.title: PriorProof: A Point-in-Time Measure of Technique Novelty for Formal Proofs

author.name: Neel Somani

entry.summary: PriorProof introduces a point-in-time measure of technique novelty for formal Lean proofs by scoring the weighted surprisal of a proof's dependency footprint under a prior built only from an earlier Mathlib snapshot. It requires no hand-built technique ontology or human labels and is validated in a blinded topology study.

entry.title: LenGuard-GPC: Length Guarding with Guided-Prompt Consistency for Spatial Reasoning Reinforce Learning

author.name: Xingjian Tao, Yiwei Wang, Yujun Cai, Jing Tang

entry.summary: LenGuard-GPC is a dense reward framework for multi-view spatial reasoning RL that compares token-wise predictive distributions under standard and guided prompts to give step-level feedback and control reasoning length. It addresses the sparse outcome-level rewards and verbosity of standard GRPO in spatial vision-language tasks.

entry.title: The Art of Not Forgetting

author.name: Ashmith Atmuri, Akshay Kumar, Yashaswini Rao Bhogarajula

entry.summary: CMP is a gradient-free architecture that encodes inputs as sparse relational codes stored in a two-tier competitive memory, trained with local updates and no backpropagation. It tests whether catastrophic forgetting stems from backprop credit assignment, reporting large improvements in backward transfer across text domains.

entry.title: Self-State Attacks on Self-Hosted AI Agents: How Far Can OS Defenses Go?

author.name: Yimeng Chen, Nathana\"el Denis, Roberto Di Pietro, J\"urgen Schmidhuber

entry.summary: This work defines self-state attacks, where a self-hosted AI agent is compromised by corrupting its own memory and configuration files via legitimate OS system calls, and characterizes a four-axis attack space. It evaluates OS resilience for prevention, detection, and recovery using live agent activity traces.

entry.title: GLidE-SLAM: GL-Accelerated Indirect-Direct Embedded SLAM

author.name: Carlos A. Pinheiro de Sousa, Heiko Hamann, Oliver Deussen

entry.summary: GLidE-SLAM is a monocular hybrid indirect-direct SLAM system that offloads GPU-accelerated direct tracking on intermediate frames while reserving the full indirect pipeline for map maintenance and global consistency. The architectural separation targets embedded deployment on drones and wearable XR devices.

entry.title: Manifold-Guided Motion Planning for Tight Assemblies

author.name: Dror Livnat, Michael M. Bilevich, Michal Kleinbort, Dan Halperin

entry.summary: CMG-RRT is a sampling-based motion planner for tight rigid-body assemblies that adaptively biases sampling toward a critical manifold, the subset of configuration space with at least one contact point, where valid near-zero-clearance solution paths lie. It targets the fundamental challenge of tight geometric constraints in assembly planning.

entry.title: PPO-HSC: An Exploratory Reinforcement Learning Framework Based on Wide-Area Policy Coverage Optimization

author.name: Yujie Shen, Haowen Chen

entry.summary: PPO-HSC adds a high-order sampling coverage reward that incentivizes discovery of low-similarity yet high-validity reasoning patterns to counter mode collapse during RLVR fine-tuning. It maintains a dynamic library of verified unique solutions to encourage exploration.

entry.title: ColGraphRAG: Late-Interaction Evidence Retrieval for Multimodal GraphRAG

author.name: Seonok Kim

entry.summary: ColGraphRAG replaces single-vector image ranking in multimodal graph-based question answering with late-interaction multi-vector scoring in the ColBERT/ColPali style, keeping the rest of the pipeline fixed. It reports improved retrieval-stage performance on MultimodalQA for graph-linked images.

entry.title: Nonuniformity Principle in Human-AI Coworking

author.name: An Luo, Jie Ding

entry.summary: This paper studies how to optimally allocate scarce human oversight across steps of AI-generated multi-step workflows, motivated by empirical observations of human-AI coworking. It proposes a nonuniformity principle indicating that oversight should be distributed unevenly across the pipeline.

entry.title: A Diagnostic Framework for AI Agent Behavior

author.name: Xichen Zhang, Yingjie Zhang, Tianshu Sun

entry.summary: This Perspective proposes layer attribution as a diagnostic framework for AI agent behavior, separating a foundational computational layer (architecture, memory, attention) from a behavioral modulation layer (identity, objectives, social and institutional structure). It aims to enable source-level diagnosis of observed agent behaviors.

entry.title: A Systematic Evaluation of Trajectory Data Curation for LoRA Fine-Tuning of Code Agents

author.name: Yunze Han

entry.summary: This paper systematically studies how trajectory quality and quantity jointly affect LoRA fine-tuning of a 7B code agent on the SWE-trajectory dataset, proposing a two-axis (efficiency and style) quality scoring framework. It runs 16 controlled experiments and uses cross-evaluation since small models attain near-zero SWE-bench resolve rates.

entry.title: Lossless but Not Free: An Empirical Anatomy of Speculative Decoding on Consumer Hardware

author.name: Param Chordiya

entry.summary: This paper provides a from-scratch, device-agnostic implementation and empirical anatomy of speculative decoding on consumer Apple-silicon hardware across five draft/target configurations. It verifies distribution equivalence at three levels and analyzes when the technique's promised speedups actually materialize.

entry.title: Depth Estimators Are Implicit Neural Fields for 3D Scene Geometry Inpainting and Reconstruction

author.name: Yingzhao Jian, Zihao Lin, Hehe Fan

entry.summary: Neural Depth Field reframes a depth estimator as a scene-level implicit field that both adapts to observed depth and fits existing geometry, enabling test-time optimization for 3D inpainting and reconstruction. The insight unifies estimation and implicit-field consistency in a single procedure.

entry.title: ConceptTree: Bringing Semantic Transparency to Black-Box Decision Making for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Yongyan Wen, Feifan Liu, Jinyi Chen, Bo An, Peng Liu, Siyuan Li

entry.summary: ConceptTree reframes high-level robotic skill selection as reasoning over human-interpretable visual concept predicates rather than opaque observation-to-action mappings. The goal is transparent, oversightable decision-making in long-horizon manipulation.

entry.title: Do Language Models Dream of Binding Molecules? Benchmarking LLMs under Spatial Constraints

author.name: Thomas MacDougall, Maksim Kuznetsov, Roman Schutski, Rim Shayakhmetov, Maxim Malkov, Vladimir Aladinskiy, Alex Aliper, Alex Zhavoronkov

entry.summary: This benchmark tests whether general-purpose LLMs can reason about 3D spatial constraints in structure-based drug design, comparing them against specialized diffusion models for pocket-conditioned ligand generation. It probes an underexplored gap in LLM physical and spatial reasoning.

entry.title: Half the Experts, All the Code: One-Shot Domain Pruning of Mixture-of-Experts LLMs for Coding

author.name: Anik Jha

entry.summary: This paper performs one-shot domain pruning of mixture-of-experts LLMs for coding, removing experts that encode never-invoked abilities so models fit on developer hardware. It reports that half the experts can be removed from two open-weight MoE models with no statistically detectable loss on coding benchmarks.

entry.title: MultiLoReFT: Decoupling Shared and Modality-Specific Subspaces in Multimodal Learning via Low-Rank Representation Fine-Tuning

author.name: Sana Tonekaboni, Viktoria Schuster, Caroline Uhler

entry.summary: MultiLoReFT extends low-rank representation fine-tuning to multimodal learning with pretrained unimodal models, decoupling shared cross-modal subspaces from modality-specific ones for interpretability and control. It avoids needing large aligned paired datasets or full end-to-end training.

entry.title: Personalized Image Aesthetic Assessment via Preference-rich Sample Mining and Cohort Merging

author.name: Zhichao Yang, Tianjiao Gu, Zhixianhe Zhang, Xiangfei Sheng, Pengfei Chen, Leida Li

entry.summary: PRAC is an MLLM-based approach to personalized image aesthetic assessment that mines preference-rich samples via collective controversy and personal deviation, then merges aesthetically resonant user cohorts. It maximizes utility from limited per-user data.

entry.title: MDND: Unsupervised Learning Guided by Non-Differentiable Refinement for Shape Correspondence

author.name: Qinsong Li, Jing Meng, Haibo Wang, Shengjun Liu

entry.summary: MDND is a deep functional map framework for shape correspondence that merges differentiable learning with a non-differentiable multiscale iterative refinement solver, overcoming the end-to-end differentiability constraint. It targets challenging non-isometric shapes.

entry.title: HCIG: A Hierarchical Cross-Modal Incongruity Graph Network for Multimodal Sarcasm and Cyberbullying Detection

author.name: Bhavana Verma, Priyanka Meel, Dinesh Kumar Vishwakarma

entry.summary: HCIG is a hierarchical cross-modal incongruity graph network for multimodal sarcasm and cyberbullying detection, modeling text-image inconsistency at token, phrase, and global levels via graph attention with learned hierarchical fusion. It targets meaning that emerges from cross-modal incongruity.

entry.title: Toward Semantic Communication for Real-time Mobile 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Fangzhou Zhao, Yao Sun, Xuesong Liu, Runze Cheng, Shang Kai, Yi Sun

entry.summary: This paper proposes a semantic communication framework for real-time mobile 3D reconstruction, transmitting compact task-critical semantics to preserve multi-view consistency and geometric estimation over unreliable links. It moves beyond image- or single-view-level SemCom designs.

entry.title: Decision Variable Analysis-Guided Differentiated Fuzzy Search for Large-Scale Multi-Objective Optimization

author.name: Boxi Xiao, Hui Bai, Jinhua Zheng, Yu Li, Juan Zou

entry.summary: DDFS is a decision-variable-analysis-guided differentiated fuzzy search method for large-scale multi-objective optimization, mapping variable roles (convergence vs diversity) to differentiated fuzzy search granularities rather than a uniform granularity. It targets high-dimensional decision spaces.

entry.title: Approximate Relative Entropy Constraints for Nonlinear Covariance Steering Under Distribution Ambiguity

author.name: Trevor N. Wolf, Jay W. McMahon

entry.summary: This paper develops a distributionally robust covariance-steering framework using relative entropy (KL divergence) to bound risk-sensitive quantities under ambiguity in the propagated state distribution for nonlinear systems. It derives computable upper bounds via a variational representation of exponential integrals.

entry.title: Disturbance-Aware Flight for Aerial Robots in Narrow Space

author.name: Lei Qiang, Tianyu He, Chenyang Sun, Xurui Liu, Miao Wang, Xiaobin Zhou

entry.summary: This work presents a disturbance-aware planning and control framework for quadrotor flight in narrow spaces, using dual-loop observers to estimate 6-DoF disturbance forces and torques in real time and folding a disturbance risk function into the planning-control loop. It moves beyond control-level-only disturbance handling.

entry.title: Configuration-Induced Passive Self-Rotation for Perception-Enhanced Autonomous Flight

author.name: Xurui Liu, Miao Wang, Tianyu He, Linrui Yang, Xiaobin Zhou

entry.summary: This letter presents a configuration-induced passively self-rotating tricopter that expands sensing field of view without extra sensors, using a rear-arm configuration parameter to regulate the self-rotation operating point and balance swept-FoV refresh against flight performance. A hierarchical autonomy framework enables agile flight.

entry.title: From Sign Language Generation to Humanoid Execution: Vision-Language Guided Retargeting with Collision Mitigation

author.name: Nabeela Khan, Bowen Wu, Runwu Shi, Benjamin Yen, Takeshi Ashizawa, Carlos Toshinori Ishi, Takashi Minato, Kazuhiro Nakadai

entry.summary: This work bridges sign-language generation outputs to humanoid execution via a volumetric SMPL-X collision-mitigation module that projects signing motions away from self-intersections and a vision-language guided retargeting pipeline. It addresses hand-hand and hand-torso penetrations that produce infeasible IK and unstable trajectories.

entry.title: InLiER: Learning-Free Heterogeneous LiDAR Place Recognition via Intermediate Mixed-Radix Structural Keypoint Tokenization

author.name: Nikolaos Stathoulopoulos, George Nikolakopoulos

entry.summary: InLiER is a learning-free heterogeneous LiDAR place-recognition pipeline that tokenizes height-sliced structural keypoints with mixed-radix token IDs encoding height, radial distance, local shape, and azimuth into a compact sub-2KB representation. The same vocabulary is reused across multi-stage retrieval for cross-sensor robustness.

entry.title: Optimal Safety Control using High-Order Control Barrier Functions

author.name: Neng Li, Zuodong Pan, Jiaxing Wang, Weiguo Xia, Wei Ren

entry.summary: This paper proposes novel high-order control barrier functions with explicitly designed safety controllers and a companion high-order control Lyapunov function, addressing compatibility between stabilization and safety objectives to establish an optimal safety controller. It contrasts its construction with existing zeroing high-order barrier functions.

entry.title: Projective Maximum Entropy: Universality and Acceptance-Region Calibration

author.name: Hideitsu Hino

entry.summary: This work formulates maximum entropy on the projective space of nonnegative measures rather than the normalized simplex, better suited to unnormalized statistical models, and proves a universality theorem showing every admissible monotone transform of the same normalized power functional shares the same optimizer under linear moment constraints. It connects admissible regions to reference-distribution deformation.

entry.title: What do I mean by “Artificial General Intelligence”?

author.name: Steven Byrnes

entry.summary: This LessWrong essay by Steven Byrnes defines what the author means by artificial general intelligence, contrasting today's task-specific AI that requires new R&D per capability with a hypothesized AGI design whose copies could autonomously learn any economic task like humans do. It is a conceptual framing piece for a broad audience.

entry.title: Attempt at Finding Alignment Faking on Llama 70B to test sleeper-agent detection generalizes

author.name: skn8733

entry.summary: This LessWrong report describes a 30-hour attempt to test whether linear-probe sleeper-agent detection generalizes to naturally arising deception by eliciting alignment faking on open-source Llama checkpoints, finding zero instances meeting the strict alignment-faking criteria across multiple behavioral tests. It is an honestly reported null result with full code and data.

entry.title: Towards surfacing model algorithms with meta-tokens in the J-Space

author.name: agam_bhatia

entry.summary: Using a J-lens on Qwen3.6-27B, the authors identify 'meta-tokens' that surface non-obvious internal computation, such as tokens firing during ambiguity, GCD/LCM arithmetic, and hedging, and show steering these tokens changes model outputs. It probes model-internal algorithms rather than just variables.

entry.title: Announcing the Corrigibility Research Fund

author.name: Max Harms

entry.summary: Max Harms announces a Corrigibility Research Fund housed at Lightcone that will award at least $200,000 in 2026 grants and prizes for corrigibility work, arguing alignment research itself remains neglected relative to evals, control, and interpretability. It is a field-building funding announcement.

entry.title: Evidence Interfaces Shape How Retrieval-Augmented Readers Use Support

author.name: Junchi Liao, Jiawen Deng, Fuji Ren

entry.summary: This paper introduces the notion of an evidence interface in multi-hop RAG, showing that a top-k answer score can conflate dropped support chains with support present in a form the reader cannot use. Using support-annotated benchmarks, it disentangles retrieval-availability failures from reader-interface effects.

entry.title: CaT-GS: Efficient 3DGS Rendering for Large Scale Scenes via Inter-frame Caching and Tile Scheduling

author.name: Tingjia Zhang, Bo Chen, Shengzhong Liu, Fan Wu, Guihai Chen

entry.summary: CaT-GS accelerates 3D Gaussian Splatting rendering for large scenes by targeting inter-frame preprocessing redundancy, viewpoint occlusion redundancy, and tile-level load imbalance via caching and tile scheduling. It aims for real-world deployment efficiency without scene re-training.

entry.title: MADA-RL: Multi-Agent Debate-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Parameter-Efficient Reasoning in Compact Models

author.name: Martino M. L. Pulici, Cuong Xuan Chu, Evgeny Kharlamov, Zifeng Ding, Volker Tresp, Yunpu Ma

entry.summary: MADA-RL specializes compact models (four billion parameters or fewer) into generator and critic roles trained with a debate-aware signal using LoRA adapters. Its key idea is a counterfactual critic advantage that rewards critics for improving over the generator ensemble's consensus.

entry.title: Enhancing Rubric-based RL via Self-Distillation

author.name: Mingxuan Xia, Yuhang Yang, Chao Ye, Shuai Zhu, Shenzhi Yang, Guangcheng Zhu, Yuhang Zhang, Cheng Peng, Haobo Wang, Siqing Wang

entry.summary: This paper improves rubric-based RL for LLMs by using self-distillation to address unexplored criteria that receive no signal and suppressed criteria that regress, while avoiding the train-inference mismatch of external guidance. It targets more reliable optimization on open-ended tasks.

entry.title: BACON: Budgeted Human Calibration for Modeling and Evaluation with Multiple AI Judges

author.name: Lei Shi, Anlan Zhang, Rita Lyu, Zhengmian Hu, Tong Yu, David Arbour, Avi Feller, Saayan Mitra, Ritwik Sinha

entry.summary: BACON is a four-stage pipeline that combines a small budget of human labels with multiple AI-judge outputs, uncertainty statistics, and embeddings to produce more accurate calibrated annotations for model ranking and quality reporting. It targets the biases of uncalibrated AI judges.

entry.title: Preference-based Antibody Expression Ranking: Scaling with Large-scale Weak Supervision

author.name: Josh Qixuan Sun, Morteza Babaie, Wenyang Hou, Mark Crowley, David Young

entry.summary: This work adapts Direct Preference Optimization to protein language models for antibody expression ranking, combining scarce quantitative expression data with large-scale weak positive supervision from immunization data via a union-masked log-likelihood and IMGT alignment. It scales to millions of unlabeled camelid antibodies.

entry.title: Scaling Limits of Constant-Stepsize SGD at Flat Minima

author.name: Jingyi Zhang, Cheng Mao, Debankur Mukherjee

entry.summary: This theoretical paper shows that constant-stepsize SGD behavior fundamentally changes at flat minima with subquadratic tails, departing from the usual square-root-alpha Gaussian scaling under Markovian noise. It proves existence, uniqueness, and geometric convergence to an augmented invariant law in a Wasserstein sense.

entry.title: Leveraging Two Robotic Arms for Tight Assembly Performance Gains

author.name: Dror Livnat, Yuval Lavi, Michael M. Bilevich, Dan Halperin

entry.summary: This paper provides an end-to-end framework for dual-arm execution of tight assembly operations from CAD models and desired relative placements, demonstrating that coordinated two-arm movement reduces average execution time by more than fifty percent versus single-arm systems with theoretical guarantees on time and accuracy. It is validated in simulation and on physical robots.

entry.title: Generative Ontology Induction: Domain-Agnostic Schema Discovery from Document Corpora Using Large Language Models

author.name: Sergei Sergienko

entry.summary: Generative Ontology Induction uses LLMs to infer a typed graph schema (entities, properties, relationships, constraints) directly from a document corpus without predefined schemas. It also introduces a Node Coverage Score metric to evaluate generated ontologies.

entry.title: Democratizing AI with Small Language Models: Structured Benchmarking and Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Local Deployment

author.name: Daniel Cersosimo

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks nine small open-weight models (135M to 3B) on a curated multiple-choice task with strict formatting and applies parameter-efficient 4-bit fine-tuning for local deployment. It frames AI democratization as selection, auditing, and specialization under realistic hardware and governance constraints.

entry.title: SEER: Supervised Learning to Control Energetic Reasoning

author.name: Sascha Van Cauwelaert, Michele Lombardi, Pierre Schaus

entry.summary: SEER uses machine learning to train an oracle that decides, per instance and dynamically at search time, whether to run expensive energetic-reasoning propagators in constraint programming. It merges static ML propagator selection with dynamic activity-based adaptation.

entry.title: Toward Anthropomorphic Dialogue: A Closed-Loop Framework for Human-Like Chat Generation, Evaluation, and Preference Alignment

author.name: Wentao Liu, Siyu Song, Xi Chen, Youjia Li, Xiaokun Wang, Min Ji, Ji Wang

entry.summary: AnthroDial is a closed-loop framework for human-like private chat that combines a persona- and memory-conditioned dialogue runtime, an executable multi-dimensional benchmark, and a post-training pipeline filtering thousands of scheduled-decision examples for SFT. It jointly targets architecture, evaluation, and preference alignment for anthropomorphic dialogue.

entry.title: Panache: One-Pass Motif Discovery at Every Window Length

author.name: Tej Sanibh Ranade

entry.summary: This paper introduces Panache, described as the first one-pass streaming algorithm for z-normalized pan matrix profile motif discovery that replaces repeated quadratic self-joins with a single near-linear scan across all window lengths. It targets the core exploratory-analysis problem of finding recurring time-series patterns of unknown duration.

entry.title: Med-OPD: Improving Medical Vision-Language Models via Evidence-Aware On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Yunhang Qian, Jiaquan Yu, Jiawei Liu, Meng Wang, Hongwei Bran Li, Xiaobin Hu

entry.summary: Med-OPD improves medical vision-language models with evidence-aware on-policy distillation that concentrates token-level supervision on sparse diagnosis-critical tokens rather than diluting them across abundant narrative tokens. It provides privacy-compatible capability transfer without redistributing raw patient data.

entry.title: LookME: Lookup-Based Multimodal Embeddings for Layer Injection in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Zeyu Xu, Xingzhong Hou, Pengkai Guo, Siling Lin, Xiao Xu, Menghua Zhai, Haoyu Chen, Yunke Zhang, Fei Huang

entry.summary: LookME extends Per-Layer Embedding lookup architectures to vision-language models by enabling multimodal embedding retrieval for layer injection, addressing the memory-latency tradeoffs of scaling dense or MoE models. It adapts ID-based text-lookup approaches to the visual modality.

entry.title: Seeing What Is Actually There: PriVE-Bench and PriVE-Tools for Counterfactual Evaluation of Agentic Visual Evidence in VLMs

author.name: Jingyu Sun, Jiachen Tu, Yuyang Xue, Yaoxin Jiang, Guoyi Xu, Zhengtao Yao, Rui Qian, Yizheng Sun, Hongpeng Zhou, Jingyuan Sun, Yan Lin

entry.summary: PriVE-Bench and PriVE-Tools evaluate whether additional visual evidence views help vision-language models reason against their language and category priors using counterfactual images. It moves beyond detecting prior-following behavior to testing agentic tool-augmented evidence-gathering as a remedy.

entry.title: PhysAgent: Reflective Agentic Physics Control for Physically Plausible Video Generation

author.name: Qirui Li, Jinkun Hao, Yibo Li, Ran Yi, Paul L. Rosin, Yu-Kun Lai

entry.summary: PhysAgent is a reflective agentic framework for physics-grounded video generation that closes the loop among physical program generation, simulation, stage-specific verification, and targeted program repair. It replaces one-shot VLM-based physics specification with iterative self-correction for finer dynamics.

entry.title: Building2Building: A Large Scale Benchmark for Generalizable Real-World Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Vincent Taboga, Justin Veilleux, Doseok Jang, Anushree Rankawat, Pierre-Luc Bacon

entry.summary: Building2Building is a large-scale reinforcement-learning benchmark of realistic HVAC control environments built on EnergyPlus with a parametric building generator, Gymnasium compatibility, and systematic variation of dynamics, action/observation spaces, and goals. It is designed to rigorously study transfer, multi-task, and meta-learning under real-world distribution shifts.

entry.title: Learning from World Feedback: Why Model Uncertainty Fails as a Risk Signal in Model-Based RL

author.name: Zhaohui Wang

entry.summary: This paper argues learning signals in safe model-based control should come from world feedback rather than internal model proxies, showing empirically that dynamics-based uncertainty penalties actually increase collision rates. It replaces the model-internal proxy with sensor-margin, time-to-collision, and outcome-supervised feedback signals.

entry.title: A Geometric Perspective on Stabilizing Value Conflict Resolution

author.name: Saket Reddy, Andy Liu

entry.summary: This paper studies how chain-of-thought reasoning helps LLMs resolve value conflicts under compressed scalar RLHF rewards, showing geometrically that CoT smooths the loss landscape in its sharpest direction. It suggests value-focused CoT may generalize to broader moral reasoning.

entry.title: Topological Signatures of Context-Level Reliability in TabPFN

author.name: James Hu, Mahdi Ghelichi

entry.summary: This study analyzes TabPFN, a transformer foundation model for tabular prediction, using zigzag persistent homology to track how internal representation topology relates to prediction reliability across synthetic tasks with known geometry. It links internal topological signatures to context-level reliability.

entry.title: Anticipate Before Acting: Future-State-Conditioned Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Lingfeng Zhang, Zhanguang Zhang, Liheng Ma, Tongtong Cao, Yingxue Zhang

entry.summary: This paper conditions vision-language navigation policies on anticipated future visual states, first showing via a privileged-input diagnostic that expert future images help select current actions, then training a policy to be predictive of future outcomes. It moves beyond next-action-only behavior cloning.

entry.title: SelectInfer: Selective Neuron Loading and Computation for On-Device LLMs

author.name: Huzaifa Shaaban Kabakibo, Eric Schniedermeyer, Artem Burchanow, Lin Wang

entry.summary: SelectInfer enables efficient on-device LLM inference through neuron-level selective loading and computation, using an offline profiler to identify task-specific and general-purpose neurons. It targets memory-constrained edge deployment without coarse pruning or retraining.

entry.title: Differentiable Logic Gate Networks for Low-Latency EEG Classification on Edge Devices

author.name: Shyamal Y. Dharia, Stephen D. Smith, Camilo E. Valderrama

entry.summary: This work compiles EEG classifiers into pure Boolean circuits via Differentiable Logic Gate Networks for low-latency edge inference, comparing against matched MLP and binarized-network baselines across four datasets. Diff-Logic outperformed the MLP on dementia screening at equal parameter budgets.

entry.title: OR Else: A Differentiable Trust Region for Policy Optimization

author.name: Chinmay Rane, Kanishka Tyagi, Michael Manry

entry.summary: This paper proposes Output Reset, a smooth one-sided saturation replacement for the clipped surrogate objective in PPO and GRPO, avoiding the abrupt derivative change of clipping. PPO-OR and GRPO-OR are tested on a small Llama model for LLM post-training.

entry.title: Simple Domain Generalization for Strong Pixel-Level Image Tampering Detection in Modern VLMs

author.name: Yi Tang, Xinyi Shang, Jiacheng Cui, Sondos Mahmoud Bsharat, Jiacheng Liu, Xiaohan Zhao, Tran Dinh Tien, Ahmed Elhagry, Salwa K. Al Khatib, Tianjun Yao, Yonina C. Eldar, Jing-Hao Xue, Hao Li, Salman Khan, Zhiqiang Shen
