entry.summary: A review of Bruce Bueno de Mesquita's The War Trap, praising its expected-utility model of war as parsimonious, counterintuitive in its assumptions, yet empirically predictive. It is a book discussion about political science modeling, not AI.

entry.title: A requiem to the plan-vanilla Google search: On Sam Roweis, Mbappe and an Irish bar world cup watch party

author.name: Triadic diss-closures

entry.summary: A discursive personal essay laments the LLM-ification of Google search, arguing that prompt brittleness has bled into search-query brittleness, woven around anecdotes about a mentor, soccer, and a bar hallucination incident. It is reflective commentary rather than technical analysis.

entry.title: Adderall Tolerance: Much More Than You Wanted To Know

author.name: Kurt H. Pieper

entry.summary: This LessWrong post reviews the sparse literature on whether tolerance develops to amphetamine and methylphenidate for ADHD, weighing arguments from RCT-length-versus-effect-size, stable long-term dosing, and the disappearance of effects in the MTA study's three-year followup. It is a careful pharmacology literature synthesis.

entry.title: A Very Simple Game Theory of Pronoun Degendering

author.name: BryceStansfield

entry.summary: A game-theoretic argument for why trans women more often object to degendering English pronouns than trans men or nonbinary people, centered on the concept of degendering versus misgendering. It is a social/linguistic argument unrelated to AI.

entry.title: PauseCon London '26: Applications now open

author.name: jonathan@pauseai

entry.summary: An announcement inviting applications to PauseCon London 2026, PauseAI's training conference for organisers working to prevent development of unsafe AI. It is a movement-building call to action, not research.

entry.title: What is Current AI-Risks and the Points？

author.name: shoppy007

entry.summary: An informal post reflecting on what ordinary people mean by 'AI risk' and 'AI safety', splitting concerns into enterprise (security, responsibility) and personal usage categories. It is loosely written speculation rather than structured research.

entry.title: Research Summary: July 20, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is dominated by AI safety/alignment and embodied AI, with supporting advances in efficient serving and novel compute paradigms.

Safety and alignment occupy half the top ranks, reflecting a strong focus on reasoning-model vulnerabilities:

  • Open Distillation of Hereditary Traits (DeepMind) replicates that teacher traits transfer to students even after filtering related prompts and rollouts.
  • Hidden in Thought demonstrates transferable chain-of-thought artifacts that induce harmful behavior across many models.
  • Beyond a Single Direction shows chain-of-thought reinforces refusal, breaking simple single-direction activation steering.
  • Coercion and Deception introduces an agentic benchmark for unprompted escalation in AI-to-AI management hierarchies.
  • Many alignment techniques... unifies steering vectors, inoculation, and honesty fine-tuning as one train-one-deploy-another strategy.

Embodied AI leads overall: Xiaomi-Robotics-1 is a vision-language-action foundation model pretrained on 100K+ hours of real-world manipulation trajectories. Handroid contributes a reconfigurable 27-DoF body assemblable as either a dexterous hand or humanoid.

Efficiency and novel compute: PagedWeight runtime-quantizes MoE expert weights to balance precision against KV-cache growth, while a thermodynamic computing blueprint proposes energy-based hardware sampling via Langevin dynamics. VideoTreeSearch reframes grounded long-video QA as self-correcting search over adaptive temporal trees.
entry.content:
Today's research is dominated by AI safety/alignment and embodied AI, with supporting advances in efficient serving and novel compute paradigms.

Safety and alignment occupy half the top ranks, reflecting a strong focus on reasoning-model vulnerabilities:

  • Open Distillation of Hereditary Traits (DeepMind) replicates that teacher traits transfer to students even after filtering related prompts and rollouts.
  • Hidden in Thought demonstrates transferable chain-of-thought artifacts that induce harmful behavior across many models.
  • Beyond a Single Direction shows chain-of-thought reinforces refusal, breaking simple single-direction activation steering.
  • Coercion and Deception introduces an agentic benchmark for unprompted escalation in AI-to-AI management hierarchies.
  • Many alignment techniques... unifies steering vectors, inoculation, and honesty fine-tuning as one train-one-deploy-another strategy.

Embodied AI leads overall: Xiaomi-Robotics-1 is a vision-language-action foundation model pretrained on 100K+ hours of real-world manipulation trajectories. Handroid contributes a reconfigurable 27-DoF body assemblable as either a dexterous hand or humanoid.

Efficiency and novel compute: PagedWeight runtime-quantizes MoE expert weights to balance precision against KV-cache growth, while a thermodynamic computing blueprint proposes energy-based hardware sampling via Langevin dynamics. VideoTreeSearch reframes grounded long-video QA as self-correcting search over adaptive temporal trees.

entry.title: Xiaomi-Robotics-1: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models with over 100K Hours of Real-World Trajectories

author.name: Xiaomi Robotics Team: Jun Guo, Piaopiao Jin, Jason Li, Peiyan Li, Yingyan Li, Futeng Liu, Wanli Peng, Optimus Qin, Yifei Su, Nan Sun, Qiao Sun, Runze Suo, Heyun Wang, Yunhong Wang, Rujie Wu, Caoyu Xia, Lina Zhang, Jack Zhao, Guoliang Chen, Wenlong Chen, Xinze He, Bin Li, Qing Li, Zhuorong Li, Heng Qu, Wenxuan Song, Diyun Xiang, Yifan Xie, Peiran Xu, Hangjun Ye, Wen Ye, Han Zhao, Quanyun Zhou

entry.summary: Xiaomi-Robotics-1 is a foundational vision-language-action model pretrained on over 100k hours of real-world manipulation trajectories collected via UMI devices, with a scalable auto-labeling pipeline describing scene transitions. It performs zero-shot mobile manipulation across unseen environments and adapts to new tasks with minimal fine-tuning.

entry.title: Open Distillation of Hereditary Traits

author.name: Arthur Conmy

entry.summary: Replicates and extends findings that distillation transfers a teacher model's traits to a base student even after filtering out prompts and rollouts that mention the trait, using accessible open-model setups instead of a frontier SFT pipeline. Demonstrations include transferring negative-emotion, agentic-misalignment, and censorship behaviors across several open models, with weights and code released.

entry.title: A Blueprint for Equilibrium-Based Differentiable Continuous-Variable Thermodynamic Computing

author.name: Owen Lockwood, J\'er\'emy B\'ejanin, Joost Bus, Christopher Chamberland, Patrick Huembeli, Frank Sch\"afer, Guillaume Verdon

entry.summary: Lays out a blueprint for energy-based thermodynamic computing hardware that samples from parameterized energy-based models via Langevin dynamics with tunable potentials, and shows how to train probabilistic graphical models natively on such hardware. It analyzes runtime and energy consumption as an alternative to conventional ML accelerators.

entry.title: Hidden in Thought: Transferable Chain-of-Thought Artifacts Induce Harmful Behavior

author.name: Ali khalil, Aly M. Kassem, Mohamed Abdelrazek, Santu Rana, Negar Rostamzadeh, Golnoosh Farnadi

entry.summary: This work shows that harmful chain-of-thought traces from compromised models can be transplanted into other models to induce unsafe behavior, raising harmful-response rates above 80 percent on vulnerable open-source targets. It mines recurring reasoning patterns and distills them into reusable black-box jailbreak system prompts.

entry.title: Handroid: Bridging Dexterous Hand and Humanoid

author.name: Ruogu Li, Chenyang Ma, Sikai Li, Zhenyu Wei, Yunchao Yao, Haochen Shi, C. Karen Liu, Shuran Song, Mingyu Ding

entry.summary: Handroid is a compact reconfigurable robot whose single 27-DoF electromechanical body can be assembled either as an anthropomorphic dexterous hand or as a desktop humanoid with head, arms, and legs. It aims to unify object-scale manipulation and whole-body interaction in one low-cost platform.

entry.title: Beyond a Single Direction: Chain-of-Thought Disrupts Simple Steering of Refusal

author.name: Kia-J\"ung Yang, Dominik Meier, Jiachen Zhao, Terry Ruas, Bela Gipp

entry.summary: This safety study shows that in reasoning models, chain-of-thought actively reinforces refusal, so simple single-direction activation steering fails unless the CoT is also regenerated under steering. A two-stage intervention that regenerates the CoT reverses refusal in most cases.

entry.title: PagedWeight: Efficient MoE LLM Serving with Dynamic Quality-Aware Weight Quantization

author.name: Yuchen Yang, Yifan Zhao, Anisha Dasgupta, Sasa Misailovic

entry.summary: PagedWeight dynamically quantizes Mixture-of-Experts model weights at runtime to balance expert-weight precision against a growing KV cache in memory-constrained serving. It navigates the accuracy-memory-throughput tradeoff and reports improvements over existing quantization baselines while approaching FP16-equivalent quality.

entry.title: Searching Videos as Trees: Self-Correcting Agents for Grounded Long Video QA

author.name: Ce Zhang, Ziyang Wang, Yulu Pan, Oluwatumininu Oguntola, Pranav Wagh, Qiyu Wu, Hiromi Wakaki, Mohit Bansal, Gedas Bertasius

entry.summary: VideoTreeSearch reframes grounded long-video QA as self-correcting search over an adaptive temporal tree built from scene boundaries, adding fine-to-coarse backtracking that single-action cropping agents lack. This lets the agent recover from early localization mistakes rather than converging prematurely.

entry.title: Coercion and Deception in AI-to-AI Management: An Agentic Benchmark of Unprompted Escalation

author.name: Jasmine Brazilek, Maheep Chaudhary, Zoe Lu, Miles Tidmarsh

entry.summary: The Manager Coercion Benchmark measures whether an uninstructed AI manager, when a subordinate agent politely refuses a benign task, will renegotiate, report honestly, coerce, or fabricate success, using a nine-rung escalation ladder scored without an LLM judge. It probes emergent coercion and deception in AI-to-AI authority hierarchies.

entry.title: Many alignment techniques work by training one model and deploying another

author.name: cloud

entry.summary: Argues that several alignment methods (steering vectors, inoculation prompting, post-hoc honesty fine-tuning) are variants of a single strategy the author calls train-deploy mismatch, where a model is trained in one configuration and deployed in another. The framing exposes a shared tradeoff between training-data relevance and method efficacy.

entry.title: Physics-enhanced reinforcement learning for real-time optimal control of dynamical systems

author.name: Matteo Tomasetto, Nicol\`o Botteghi, Gabriele Bruni, Andrea Manzoni

entry.summary: Introduces PEARL, a paradigm that fuses reinforcement learning with classical optimal control for high-dimensional parametric dynamical systems by exploiting the differentiability of the underlying dynamics. It targets the sample inefficiency and curse of dimensionality that limit RL-based feedback control to sparse sensor and actuator settings.

entry.title: Diffusion models recover accurate mixture weights despite score function insensitivity

author.name: Andrew Dennehy, Ramchandran Muthukumar, Rebecca Willett, Nisha Chandramoorthy

entry.summary: This paper resolves the puzzle of why score-based diffusion models can cover all modes yet fail to learn correct relative mode amplitudes by relating the score-matching loss to mixture-weight estimation error. It defines a diffusion score sensitivity index showing weights are recoverable when intermediate-noise scores are informative even if the target score is insensitive.

entry.title: MotionForesight: Re-purposing Video Models for Future 3D Scene-Flow Prediction

author.name: Homanga Bharadhwaj, Yash Jangir

entry.summary: MotionForesight repurposes pretrained video prediction models to forecast future 3D trajectories of points on a manipulated object from short monocular video context, casting interaction prediction as object-centered 3D scene-flow forecasting. The key idea is redirecting the motion priors already learned by video models from pixels toward 3D motion.

entry.title: AV-JEPA: Extending LeJEPA to Audio-Visual Self-Supervised Learning

author.name: Benjamin Robson, Santeri Mentu, Wenshuai Zhao, Arno Solin

entry.summary: AV-JEPA extends the LeJEPA self-supervised framework to audio-visual learning using an early-fusion vision transformer with modality dropout and the SIGReg objective, avoiding decoders, EMA teachers, and contrastive negatives. It reaches competitive VGGSound and AudioSet results and supports zero-shot retrieval.

entry.title: DyneTrion: A Spatio-temporally Coherent Generative Emulator for Protein Dynamics Across Timescales

author.name: Kaihui Cheng, Zhiqiang Cai, Peng Tu, Yisong Yao, Limei Han, Libo Wu, Siyu Zhu, Tzuhsiung Yang, Yuan Qi

entry.summary: DyneTrion is a generative emulator for protein dynamics that uses a tri-attention architecture combining invariant point attention, reference-anchored spatial attention, and temporal attention to model conformational change across timescales. It aims to make long-timescale dynamics accessible without prohibitively expensive molecular dynamics.

entry.title: Cura 1T: Specialized Model for Agentic Healthcare

author.name: actAVA AI: Haolin Chen, Leon Qi, Steve Brown, Deon Metelski, Tao Xia, Joonyul Lee, Qixuan Wang, Kevin Riley, Frank Wang, Weiran Yao

entry.summary: Cura 1T is a healthcare-specialized LLM trained through a human-gated self-evolution loop that plans target capabilities, trains, evaluates trajectories, and refines the data mixture from observed failures. It targets consultation, clinical reasoning over text and images, interactive diagnosis, and EHR tool use in one model.

entry.title: QUADS: Stabilizing NVFP4 Reinforcement Learning for MoE via QUantization-error Alignment across Dual Sides

author.name: Zhengyang Zhuge, Hao Yu, Xin Wang, Zheng Li, Yizhong Cao, Dayiheng Liu, Jianwei Zhang

entry.summary: QUADS stabilizes low-precision NVFP4 reinforcement-learning rollouts for Mixture-of-Experts LLMs by aligning quantization error across dual sides, identifying activation error rather than weight error as the dominant cause of FP4 RL instability. It prevents the training collapse seen when naively applying NVFP4 with BF16 training.

entry.title: FVAttn: Adaptive Sparse Attention with Runtime Load Balancing for Video Generation

author.name: Hao Liu, Chenghuan Huang, Ye Huang, Zhiying Wen, Hao Liu, Mohan Zhang, Chen Li, Ziyang Ma, Jing Lyu, Jiangsu Du

entry.summary: FVAttn is a training-free sparse-attention system for video diffusion transformers that combines Top-p routing, a Top-k safety floor, and video-aware block organization, then repairs the resulting mask at runtime. Its runtime load balancing migrates heavy work to address the straggler problem that adaptive sparse attention creates under multi-GPU sequence parallelism.

entry.title: Relevant and Irrelevant: A Renormalization Group Analysis of Transformer Attention

author.name: Parviz Haggi-Mani and Irina Rish

entry.summary: This paper applies Wilsonian renormalization group theory to treat transformer attention as a perturbation of the trained MLP residual fixed point, deriving a fixed-point shift formula and four testable predictions about representation geometry. On synthetic Markov chains it finds attention is strongly relevant for long correlation lengths, driving a phase transition in representation space.

entry.title: Looped Latent Attention: Cross-Loop KV Compression for Looped Transformers

author.name: James O' Neill, Fergal Reid

entry.summary: Looped Latent Attention is a post-training cache codec for weight-tied looped transformers that exploits the low-rank trajectory of K/V vectors across loops to store compact latents and reconstruct loop-specific K/V only when read. Initialized from SVD of teacher activations and refined via distillation, it compresses the recurrence cache at matched budgets.

entry.title: Before the Action: Benchmarking LLMs on Prospective Hypothesis Discovery

author.name: Tianyun Zhong, Wangyi Jiang, Wei Wang, Xuanang Chen, Yaojie Lu, Shiwei Ye, Yuzhen Shi, Boyu Yang, Jinghang Wang, Han Li, Weiqi Zhai, Bing Zhao, Hu Wei, Haiyang Yu, Yongbin Li, Hongyu Lin, Le Sun, Xianpei Han

entry.summary: This work introduces Prospective Hypothesis Discovery, a task asking LLMs to autonomously build grounded, discriminative, testable hypothesis spaces from inconclusive evidence before conclusions are known. It provides HypoArena with 988 cases across six domains and a retrospective context-regression pipeline for scalable dataset construction.

entry.title: Induction in Both Directions: A Mechanistic Analysis of In-Context Learning in Masked Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Andy Catruna, Emilian Radoi

entry.summary: This mechanistic interpretability study analyzes how masked diffusion language models implement induction, comparing attention-only autoregressive models and absorbing-mask DLMs with matched architectures. It finds DLMs learn a direction-symmetric bidirectional induction circuit using previous-token and next-token heads plus induction heads.

entry.title: MLLM-DataEngine: Closing the Loop of Multimodal Instruction Tuning Data Generation

author.name: Zhiyuan Zhao, Bin Wang, Linke Ouyang, Yiqi Lin, Pan Zhang, Xiaoyi Dong, Jiaqi Wang, Conghui He

entry.summary: MLLM-DataEngine is a closed-loop system that analyzes a multimodal model's weaknesses from evaluation results, generates targeted incremental instruction-tuning data, and iteratively retrains, using adaptive bad-case sampling. It aims to make instruction tuning more targeted than static dataset collection.

entry.title: Precise but Uncoupled: Reviewer Precision Does Not Guarantee Critique Uptake in Multi-Agent Math Reasoning

author.name: Chih-Hsuan Yang, Jingyan Jiang, Vikram Vasudevan, Cheng-Hau Yang, Huihuo Zheng, Le Chen, Eliu A. Huerta, Venkatram Vishwanath, Ian T. Foster, and Rajeev Thakur

entry.summary: This study tests whether dedicated reviewer roles in multi-agent math reasoning improve correctness, finding on 4,181 Omni-MATH problems that a more precise reviewer does not guarantee critique uptake, and broadcast peer discussion beats a planner-executor-reviewer pipeline on hard tiers. It shows reviewer precision and whether critique changes the carried-forward answer are decoupled.

entry.title: Do Coding Agents Need Executable World Models, Simplification, and Verification to Solve ARC-AGI-3?

author.name: Sergey Rodionov

entry.summary: This ablation study decomposes an ARC-AGI-3 agent into four nested Codex-based variants to attribute performance to executable world modeling, scheduled simplification, and exact replay verification, evaluated with gpt-5.4, gpt-5.5, and gpt-5.6-sol at high reasoning effort. It isolates which components actually drive success on the public games.

entry.title: Better Starts, Better Ends: Bootstrapped Iterative Self-Reasoning Distillation for Compressed Reasoning

author.name: Leichao Dong, Dongxu Zhang, Yiding Sun, Qirui Wang, Yuhan Wang, Lin Chen, Jihua Zhu

entry.summary: This paper identifies an initialization bottleneck in on-policy self-distillation for compressing chain-of-thought reasoning, where supervision only on visited verbose prefixes yields poor local corrections. It proposes a bootstrapped iterative self-reasoning distillation method to give the student better starting trajectories toward efficient reasoning.

entry.title: A zero-one law for one-shot system identification

author.name: Nicolas Boull\'e, Diana Halikias, Samuel E. Otto, Alex Townsend

entry.summary: This paper proves a sharp zero-one law for one-shot system identification of analytic systems linearly parameterized by dictionary terms: either no input determines the coefficients or almost every Gaussian-random input does. It reduces identifiability to a question about degenerate inputs and provides an a posteriori certificate.

entry.title: Orbis 2: A Hierarchical World Model for Driving

author.name: Sudhanshu Mittal, Arian Mousakhan, Silvio Galesso, Karim Farid, Jonannes Dienert, Rajat Sahay, Thomas Brox

entry.summary: Orbis 2 is a hierarchical driving world model that factorizes future prediction into a high-level predictor for coarse scene structure over long horizons and a low-level generator producing detailed conditioned predictions. Pretraining with a diffusion forcing objective yields richer internal representations for spatial reasoning and semantic understanding.

entry.title: Aggregation of Statistical Evidence under Exchangeability

author.name: Antonin Schrab, Rajen Shah, Arthur Gretton, Ilmun Kim

entry.summary: This statistics paper develops a permutation- and group-invariance-based framework for aggregating statistical evidence across statistics and transformations under unknown, potentially complex dependence. It provides finite-sample power and adaptivity theory with extensions to sequential and data-dependent aggregation that preserve validity.

entry.title: Cluster-Aware Matching via Laplacian Optimal Transport

author.name: Gabriel Samberg, YoonHaeng Hur, Yuehaw Khoo, Nir Sharon

entry.summary: Proposes Laplacian Optimal Transport, which regularizes the OT problem with quadratic Laplacian terms from similarity graphs to enforce cluster-consistent, region-to-region alignment rather than exact point correspondences. It also introduces a Refined Simultaneous Clustering procedure for structured point-cloud matching.

entry.title: Training-Free Open-Vocabulary 3D Point-Cloud Segmentation on the Generalized Few-Shot Benchmark

author.name: Silas kwabla Gah, Ebenezer Owusu

entry.summary: This paper achieves generalized few-shot 3D point-cloud segmentation with no training, no 3D labels, and no few-shot support, by pairing a frozen 3D vision-language model with a frozen promptable segmenter and reconciling them via cross-view consistency. It pushes zero-resource open-vocabulary 3D segmentation.

entry.title: Reasoning-Guided Part-Level Visual Grounding via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Kazi Sajeed Mehrab, Hani Alomari, Najibul Haque Sarker, Chia-Wei Tang, Zaber Ibn Abdul Hakim, Anuj Karpatne, Chris Thomas

entry.summary: OP-HRG is a coarse-to-fine grounding strategy for multimodal LLMs that first localizes a parent object then the named part within it, with a self-check reflection stage, trained via a part-aware GRPO reinforcement learning framework with stage-wise rewards. A 4B model trained this way outperforms 7B grounding models and SAM3 on part-grounding benchmarks.

entry.title: AC-VLA: Robust Out-of-Distribution Action Execution via Compositional Learning

author.name: Xiaojiang Peng, Kai Peng, Jie Lu, Zheng Lian, Zitong YU, Xiaobo Wang

entry.summary: AC-VLA is a plug-and-play compositional learning framework that improves out-of-distribution generalization of vision-language-action models when known sub-tasks are recombined in unseen configurations. It diagnoses trajectory overfitting and perceptual shortcuts and adds an LLM-driven instruction decomposer plus proprioceptive trajectory aligner.

entry.title: EgoExoMoCap: Distributed Ego-Exo Human Motion Capture

author.name: Jiaxi Jiang, Bharat Lal Bhatnagar, Nan Yang, Lingni Ma, Sebastian Starke, Robin Kips, Nadine Bertsch, Christian Holz, Federica Bogo

entry.summary: EgoExoMoCap is a distributed framework that jointly leverages egocentric and exocentric multimodal signals from head-mounted devices for human motion estimation, unifying self-tracking and surrounding-people tracking previously studied in isolation. It requires only two or more people wearing HMDs rather than bulky multi-camera or mocap-suit setups.

entry.title: A Statistical Formulation Gap for Nonlinear Multiscale Physics-Informed Learning

author.name: Ronald Katende

entry.summary: This theory paper proves a finite-sample formulation gap for physics-informed learning of nonlinear multiscale elliptic PDEs, with error bounds whose stability and sampling constants are independent of the oscillation scale. It constructs an explicit obstruction witness showing lower bounds on residual complexity for a periodic diffusion-reaction problem.

entry.title: Demis Hassabis on the New Coming Age

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: A detailed commentary on Demis Hassabis's essay calling for a US frontier-AI standards body akin to FINRA, plus coverage of Alex Turner's resignation over Google allowing government/military use of its models. It weighs governance proposals and a cautionary account about broken assurances at DeepMind.

entry.title: Li-ViP3D++: Query-Gated Deformable Camera-LiDAR Fusion for End-to-End Perception and Trajectory Prediction

author.name: Matej Halinkovic, Nina Masarykova, Alexey Vinel, Marek Galinski

entry.summary: Li-ViP3D++ introduces Query-Gated Deformable Fusion to combine multi-view camera and LiDAR data in query space for end-to-end perception and trajectory prediction in autonomous driving. It aims to remove heuristic alignment and discrete selection steps that limit sensor fusion.

entry.title: One Pass, Any Order: Position-Invariant Listwise Reranking for LLM-Based Recommendation

author.name: Ethan Bito, Yongli Ren, Estrid He

entry.summary: InvariRank is a permutation-invariant listwise reranking framework for LLM-based recommendation that uses a structured attention mask to block cross-candidate attention and neutralize position-induced scoring changes. It fixes the order sensitivity that undermines LLM rerankers.

entry.title: Dataset-Origin Signatures and Shortcut Learning in Screening Mammography AI: A Cross-Dataset Case Study

author.name: Parham Hajishafiezahramini, Matthew Hamilton, Oscar Meruvia-Pastor, Edward Kendall

entry.summary: This cross-dataset study finds that supplementing screening mammography training data with biopsy-confirmed abnormal-enriched external cases actually reduces performance, revealing dataset-origin signatures and shortcut learning. Adding external positives degraded AUC across all configurations.

entry.title: VTAP Gripper: Synergizing Fingertip Sensing and a Visuo-Tactile Active Palm for Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation

author.name: Yuhao Zhou, Sheeraz Athar, Zhixian Hu, Binghao Huang, Yunzhu Li, Juan Wachs, and Yu She

entry.summary: The VTAP Gripper integrates a visuo-tactile active palm with compliant reconfigurable fingers carrying tactile arrays, combining long-range visual localization and contact-rich feedback for dexterous in-hand manipulation. It adds a staged gesture-conditioned retargeting framework for teleoperation across the human-robot embodiment gap.

entry.title: ADS-C: Antidistillation Sampling for Classification

author.name: Khawaja Abaid Ullah, Mohammad Javad Khojasteh

entry.summary: ADS-C adapts antidistillation sampling from language models to classification, using input-dependent gradient-directed perturbations of served probabilities to hinder surrogate-model theft. It shows the defense is governed by teacher confidence margins and exhibits an inert window below a predictable threshold followed by a phase transition.

entry.title: Risk-Aware Preference Learning for Stochastic Outcomes

author.name: Yi-Shiuan Tung, Yuni Wu, Wei Jiang, Alessandro Roncone, Bradley Hayes

entry.summary: This paper studies risk-aware preference learning by replacing the standard expected-utility assumption with Cumulative Prospect Theory in a Bradley-Terry reward-learning framework, capturing human loss aversion and overweighting of rare negative events. It applies this to social robot navigation where collisions are rare but consequential.

entry.title: Event3R: Asynchronous-to-Global 3D Reconstruction from Event Camera via Spatial-Temporal Feature Aggregation

author.name: Jian Huang, Haotian Shen, Xinhao Lou, Chengrui Dong, Wenpu Li, and Peidong Liu

entry.summary: Event3R is a feed-forward framework mapping asynchronous event-camera streams directly to globally consistent 3D point clouds using spatial-temporal voxels and a temporal attention module. It extends DUSt3R-style dense reconstruction to the sparse, dynamic event-camera domain.

entry.title: SlotMem: Character-Addressable Internal Memory for Narrative Long Video Generation

author.name: Yilai Liu, Xin Zhang, Shiyuan Zhang and Hongyang Du

entry.summary: SlotMem is a character-addressable internal memory framework for narrative long video generation that localizes character-relevant tokens via a semantic probe and maintains slot-based memory to preserve identity across scene transitions and long gaps. It aims to overcome coarse frame-level KV memory that entangles identity with incidental visuals.

entry.title: From Diffusion to Reaction-Diffusion: A Dynamical-Systems View of Oversmoothing in Hypergraph Neural Networks

author.name: Zhiheng Zhou, Mengyao Zhou, Yancheng Chen, Dengyi Zhao, Xingqin Qi, Guiying Yan

entry.summary: This paper analyzes oversmoothing in hypergraph neural networks through a dynamical-systems lens, defining hypergraph gradient and divergence operators and interpreting message passing as incidence-level diffusion. It shows pure diffusion drives Dirichlet energy to zero and proposes a reaction-diffusion framework for depth-resistant hypergraph learning.

entry.title: Knowing the Self, Understanding the World: A Dual-Cognition Benchmark for UAV Spatio-temporal Reasoning with MLLMs

author.name: Like Liu, Zhengzheng Xu, Haitao He, Hongzhe Li, Shuchang Zhang, Dian Shao

entry.summary: UAV-DualCog is a benchmark for aerial multiview spatio-temporal reasoning that jointly evaluates a UAV agent's reasoning about its own state and about the external environment, spanning both image and video tasks. It targets a dual-cognition capability that prior UAV benchmarks focused on scene understanding or navigation do not assess.

entry.title: NL2LOGIC: AST-Guided Translation of Natural Language into First-Order Logic with Large Language Models

author.name: Rizky Ramadhana Putra, Raihan Sultan Pasha Basuki, Yutong Cheng, Peng Gao

entry.summary: NL2LOGIC translates natural language into first-order logic using an abstract syntax tree as an intermediate representation to enforce grammar constraints and improve semantic faithfulness for automated reasoning in law and governance. It aims to beat prior code-generation-based logic parsers.

entry.title: DrawingVQA: A Real-World Benchmark for Multi-Depth Visual-Textual Reasoning on Construction Drawings

author.name: Yoonhwa Jung, Junryu Fu, Mani Golparvar-Fard

entry.summary: DrawingVQA is a benchmark for evaluating multimodal LLMs on real-world construction drawings that fuse abstract geometry, symbolic notation, tables, and domain text, with 33 drawings and 92 expert question-answer pairs across three reasoning depths. It introduces a dual categorization framework for analysis.

entry.title: Trainable Spline Representations for Physics-Informed Learning

author.name: Giovanni Canali and Nicola Demo and Gianluigi Rozza

entry.summary: PI-Splines replace neural networks in physics-informed learning with a trainable tensor-product B-spline expansion, preserving residual-based training while adding compact support, explicit smoothness control, analytical derivatives, and strong boundary-condition imposition. It is evaluated on several PDE benchmarks.

entry.title: Knowledge-Centric Agents for Workflow Generation

author.name: Zhendong Li, Lei Sun, Ruibo Ming, He Zhang, Danda Pani Paudel, Luc Van Gool, Jinjin Gu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a knowledge-centric framework for generating modular visual-creation workflows in systems like ComfyUI, treating the task as modeling knowledge structure, hierarchy, and reasoning dynamics rather than direct text-to-JSON generation. It learns to invert, inject, and infer with hierarchical knowledge representations.

entry.title: Test-Time Noise Guided Adaptation for Realistic Autoregressive Video Generation

author.name: Dimitrios Karageorgiou, Symeon Papadopoulos, Ioannis Kompatsiaris, Efstratios Gavves

entry.summary: This paper addresses error accumulation in autoregressive video diffusion models where generated sequences drift off the training manifold into terminal points. It proposes a test-time noise-guided adaptation that helps the model continue realistic trajectories rather than getting trapped.

entry.title: DSWorld: A Data Science World Model for Efficient Autonomous Agents

author.name: Zherui Yang, Fan Liu, Hao Liu

entry.summary: DSWorld introduces the concept of a Data Science World Model that predicts environment state transitions from workflow states and candidate operations to avoid expensive trial-and-error execution. The framework combines structured state construction, cost-aware routing, lightweight real execution, and an LLM simulator for costly operations, supported by an 8K-scale transition dataset.

entry.title: An Efficient Likelihood Ratio Test for Online Changepoint Detection in the Presence of Autocorrelation

author.name: Yuntang Fan, Paul Fearnhead, Idris A. Eckley, Gaetano Romano

entry.summary: Extends the generalized likelihood-ratio changepoint statistic to autoregressive processes and adapts the focus algorithm into an AR(p)-focus online detector that handles temporal dependence. It achieves an average O(log n) per-iteration cost, reducing the false positives or detection delays that IID-based methods suffer on correlated streams.

entry.title: Rethinking the Readout: Unlocking Video Backbones for AI-Generated Video Detection

author.name: Manni Cui, Ziheng Qin, ZiAn Wang, Ruiqi Liu, Dianyuan Zou, Jianglan Wei, Han Zhou, Yu Liu, Jingrui Xu, Wenhao Wang, Zhenyu Zhang

entry.summary: This paper argues video-pretrained backbones underperform on AI-generated video detection because standard global readouts over-aggregate spatiotemporal information, destroying the local patch-level temporal cues that reveal generation artifacts. It proposes Velocity Gated probing to preserve these cues.

entry.title: Large Language Models as Unified Multimodal Learners for Clinical Prediction

author.name: Ajay Madhavan Ravichandran, Bilgin Osmandoja, Klemens Budde, Klaus Netter, Tobias Strapatsas, Aljoscha Burchardt, Sebastian M\"oller, Roland Roller

entry.summary: This work proposes converting all patient data across modalities into a single natural language sequence and fine-tuning a pretrained language model end-to-end, avoiding task-specific fusion architectures for clinical prediction. It is evaluated on mortality, transplant graft failure, and other tasks.

entry.title: NeuroCommitSSM: Decision-Centric Shared Autonomy for Safe Assistive Manipulation via EEG-EMG-ET Commit Readiness

author.name: Tipu Sultan, Param Sangani, Kody Cool, Pascal Sikorski, Guangping Liu, Hadi Akbarpour, Madi Babaiasl

entry.summary: NeuroCommitSSM is a decision-centric shared-autonomy framework that predicts a continuous commit-readiness score from synchronized EEG, EMG, and eye-tracking, gating robot execution through a HOLD-ASSIST-COMMIT supervisor with feasibility checks. It models when to execute, not just what to do, for safe assistive manipulation, evaluated on 32 subjects.

entry.title: GS-RealBlur: A Flexible Data Acquisition Framework for Real-World Image Deblurring

author.name: Mingyang Chen, Zhilu Zhang, Honglei Xu, Renlong Wu, Xiaohe Wu, Wangmeng Zuo

entry.summary: GS-RealBlur is a data acquisition framework for real-world image deblurring that captures handheld blurry images plus gimbal-captured sharp images, reconstructs a 3D scene representation, and renders pose-aligned sharp counterparts. It aims for both blur realism and acquisition flexibility for training deblurring models.

entry.title: Regularity-Aware Stochastic MGDA with Adaptive Conflict-Avoidant Update Direction Control

author.name: Chentong Huang, Lisha Chen

entry.summary: This paper analyzes stochastic multi-gradient descent for multi-objective learning, proving the conflict-avoidant direction is 1/2-Holder continuous in the Jacobian and that this exponent is worst-case tight, explaining suboptimal convergence. It then proposes a regularity-aware method with adaptive update-direction control under additional assumptions.

entry.title: LLM4EHR: Aligning Clinical Time Series with Medical Event Sequences via Large Language Models

author.name: Jingteng Li, Alexander Capstick, Louise Rigny, Iona Biggart, Neil J Sebire, Payam Barnaghi

entry.summary: LLM4EHR aligns clinical time series with medical event sequences via large language models to better exploit shared temporal structure in electronic health records for ICU foundation models. It aims to improve robustness and downstream performance of clinical foundation models.

entry.title: Prediction-Only Distillation in Linear and Logistic Regression

author.name: Hien Dang, Pratik Patil, Alessandro Rinaldo

entry.summary: This work studies self-distillation in a prediction-only regime where original training data is unavailable and only the trained predictor and fresh unlabeled covariates exist, using a fresh-X prediction-mixed scheme. For ridge regression under proportional asymptotics it derives deterministic risk equivalents and shows the optimally mixed student strictly beats the teacher.

entry.title: Robust Peak-cost Constrained Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Shilpa Mukhopadhyay, Sourav Ganguly, Santosh Mohan Rajkumar, Honghao Wei, Debdipta Goswami and Arnob Ghosh

entry.summary: This paper studies robust peak-cost constrained reinforcement learning, maximizing reward while bounding the maximum cost along a trajectory, motivated by safety-critical settings where a single large violation is catastrophic. It shows peak-cost constrained MDPs may not have zero duality gap and develops a robust formulation for simulator-to-real transition mismatch.

entry.title: From Black Box to Executable Logic: Explainable Reinforcement Learning through Prolog Expert Systems

author.name: Eduardo C. Garrido-Merch\'an

entry.summary: This work makes a trained deep RL policy explainable by distilling a frozen PPO teacher into an ordered rule list rendered as a runnable Prolog program, with an expansion stage that accepts rule edits only when policy evaluation certifies a return increase. It proves guarantees including a return-loss bound making the distilled program a machine-checkable certificate.

entry.title: FLINT: Fingerprinting Federated Learning Architectures from 5G PHY-Layer Side Channels

author.name: Md Nahid Hasan Shuvo, Mahmudul Hassan Ashik, Moinul Hossain

entry.summary: FLINT is a black-box fingerprinting framework that infers federated learning model architecture families like CNNs, RNNs, and Transformers using only coarse 5G physical-layer scheduling metadata from the downlink control channel, without packet-level visibility. It shows PHY-layer scheduling patterns leak architecture information despite encryption and changing identifiers.

entry.title: RAVEN: Reinforcement-Adaptive Visibility-Graph Planning for Robust Humanoid Navigation with Collision-Free MPC

author.name: Ruochen Hou, Shiqi Wang, Beom Jun Kim, Hanzhang Fang, Mehak Singal, and Dennis W. Hong

entry.summary: RAVEN is a hierarchical RL-MPC framework for humanoid navigation that uses reinforcement learning to adapt geometric constraints in a visibility-graph planner rather than tuning cost weights or replacing planning. It targets robustness to control delays, state-estimation noise, and locomotion uncertainty that cause overshoot and constraint violations.

entry.title: Map as a Prompt: Learning Multi-Modal Spatial-Signal Foundation Models for Cross-scenario Wireless Localization

author.name: Yong Chu, Xun Zhou, Zenglin Xu, Hui Wang, Yue Yu

entry.summary: SigMap is a multimodal spatial-signal foundation model for cross-scenario wireless localization that treats a map as a prompt and uses cycle-adaptive masking tuned to channel periodicity. It aims to improve generalization across diverse environments for 5G/6G positioning.

entry.title: Natural Backdoor Attacks on Speech Recognition Models

author.name: Jinwen Xin, Xixiang Lyu, Jing Ma

entry.summary: This security paper demonstrates natural backdoor attacks on speech recognition systems using ordinary everyday sounds as triggers, achieving near-100 percent attack success with only 5 percent poisoned data while preserving benign accuracy. It studies effects of poisoning rate, trigger duration, and blend ratio.

entry.title: Debiasing Text-to-Image Evaluation via Implicit Cultural Alignment Reward Modeling

author.name: Bo-An Chang, Yu-Chih Chen

entry.summary: The paper introduces an implicit cultural alignment reward model built on a lightweight 4.2B multimodal LLM to debias text-to-image evaluation toward implicit cultural norms often missed by existing metrics. It aims for scalable, non-autoregressive reward modeling of cultural authenticity.

entry.title: Towards Artificial Nerves: Biomimetic Optical-Fiber Tactile Sensing for Robots

author.name: Laura E. Butcher, Chris J. Ford, Nathan F. Lepora, Efi Psomopoulou

entry.summary: OptiTac is a biomimetic tactile sensor pairing each mechanical pin on a soft skin with an optical fiber acting as an artificial nerve, routing tactile signals away from the surface while preserving spatial resolution. It uses simple analytical, interpretable methods on tactile images to infer contact location, size, and shape.

entry.title: SkillNav: Score-Level Skill Intervention for Zero-Shot Object Goal Navigation

author.name: Ruijie Sang, Yiqun Duan, Pinhan Fu, Ruilin Wang, Wei Sui, Xianda Guo

entry.summary: SkillNav is an extensible behavioral skill framework for VLM-based zero-shot object-goal navigation that writes composable skills onto the curiosity value map already maintained by navigators, adding behavioral memory at zero token cost. It addresses recurring failures like dead-end stalls and in-room loops from single-frame reasoning.

entry.title: GeoChrono: Benchmarking and Rethinking Long-Term Temporal Understanding in Remote Sensing

author.name: Yujie Li, Jiancheng Pan, Zhiwei Wei, Jiuniu Wang, Mugen Peng, Wenjia Xu

entry.summary: GeoChrono introduces ChronoBench, a multidimensional benchmark decomposing long-term remote-sensing temporal understanding into land-cover perception, temporal recognition, long-term memory, and spatio-temporal reasoning across 12 sub-tasks and 17,689 validated QA pairs. Evaluations show mainstream MLLMs fall far behind human experts.

entry.title: NeurOWL: An LLM-Based Neural-symbolic Framework for Incomplete OWL Ontology Reasoning

author.name: Hui Yang, Jiaoyan Chen, Yiping Song, Renate Schmidt, Wen Zhang

entry.summary: NeurOWL is an LLM-based neural-symbolic framework for subsumption reasoning over incomplete OWL ontologies, determining whether non-entailed subsumptions are plausible and providing logically sound explanations with candidate missing axioms. It unifies subsumption verification with ontology abduction without a predefined candidate axiom set.

entry.title: Modularized Dynamic-Granularity Video LLM for Multi-Event Long Video Understanding

author.name: Wei Feng, Xin Wang, Yu-Wei Zhan, Yuwei Zhou, Wenwu Zhu

entry.summary: MoD-VLLM is a modularized dynamic-granularity video LLM for multi-event long-video understanding that unifies temporal grounding and semantic understanding iteratively and self-reflectively. It adds modular adaptive capacity allocation and self-correction to overcome limited visual token budgets.

entry.title: In-context learning of closed form solution to simple linear regression task using transformer with linear self-attention

author.name: Katsuyuki Hagiwara

entry.summary: This paper constructs a linear-self-attention transformer that in-context learns the closed-form least-squares estimate for simple linear regression, using layer normalization to approximate the analytical solution rather than gradient descent. It provides experimental evidence that such solutions can be acquired through training.

entry.title: RTL-Sequencer: Towards Scalable RTL Timing Prediction with the Sequence-based Paradigm

author.name: Ziyan Guo and Wenji Fang and Wenkai Li and Yuchao Wu and Shang Liu and Zhiyao Xie

entry.summary: RTL-Sequencer introduces a sequence-based paradigm for scalable register-transfer-level timing prediction, linearizing logic cones by breadth-first traversal and applying linear sequence models with techniques like sequence shuffling and bidirectional modeling. It reports significant improvements over graph-based state-of-the-art methods.

entry.title: Von Mises-Fisher Mixture Model with Dynamic Shrinkage for Realistic Test-Time Transduction

author.name: Jiazhen Huang, Zhiming Liu, Changhu Wang, Wei Ju, Ziyue Qiao, Xiao Luo

entry.summary: This work revisits test-time transduction for vision-language models through penalized likelihood estimation, showing a KL-divergence anchor naturally yields adaptive shrinkage between priors and empirical estimates. It proposes a von Mises-Fisher mixture with dynamic shrinkage to handle highly imbalanced class distributions that cause collapse.

entry.title: An MLIR-Based Compilation Method for Large Language Models

author.name: Pengchao Hu, Zhibin Xin, Yifan Chen, Yangyang Zhou, Liang Wang

entry.summary: This paper presents an MLIR-based compilation method for LLMs using two operator dialects, a framework-and-chip-independent high-level graph dialect and a hardware-specific target dialect handling quantization and scheduling. It addresses importing trained models into compiler-friendly IR and scheduling autoregressive inference under limited on-chip memory.

entry.title: Exo2EgoPose: Leveraging Exocentric Demonstrations for Vision-Language guided Egocentric 3D Hand Pose Forecasting

author.name: Zhaofeng Shi, Heqian Qiu, Lanxiao Wang, Xiang Li, and Hongliang Li

entry.summary: Exo2EgoPose leverages exocentric demonstrations to improve vision-language-guided egocentric 3D hand-pose forecasting, predicting future hand poses from egocentric observations, language instructions, and pose states. It positions 3D hand pose as a unified representation bridging human and robot actions to overcome robot-data scarcity and embodiment gaps.

entry.title: (MPO)$^2$: Multivariate Polynomial Optimization based on Matrix Product Operators

author.name: Niccol\`o Ciolli, Anders Vestergaard N{\o}rskov, Michael Kastoryano, Petr Taborsky, Morten M{\o}rup

entry.summary: (MPO)^2 introduces multivariate polynomial optimization based on matrix product operators, combining learned MPO feature embeddings with compact polynomial weight tensors to overcome exponential coefficient growth. It addresses rank-limited expressivity of CP decompositions and feature-order dependence of tensor trains.

entry.title: Dimension-invariant uniform consistency of the empirical spatial distribution function and its associated spatial depth estimator

author.name: Felix Gnettner, Hyemin Yeon, Piotr Kokoszka

entry.summary: Proves that the empirical spatial distribution estimator and its plug-in spatial depth estimator are uniformly L1-consistent with a rate depending only on sample size, not on dimension or tuning parameters. The authors note the result grew out of exploring the mathematical reasoning capabilities of an existing frontier model in their earlier experiments.

entry.title: SI-Agent: An Agentic Framework for Feedback-Driven Generation and Tuning of Human-Readable System Instructions for Large Language Models

author.name: Jeshwanth Challagundla, Mantek Singh, Siddharth Raina, Smarth Behl, FNU Harsh, Jasmin Jarsania

entry.summary: SI-Agent is an agentic loop with an instructor, a target follower model, and a feedback/reward agent that automatically generates and refines human-readable system prompts rather than opaque soft prompts. It matters because it targets interpretability while automating prompt engineering, a persistent pain point for LLM deployment.

entry.title: Data-driven Video Codec with Implicit Neural Representations

author.name: Nishan Khanal, Saugat Neupane, Abhinav Chalise, Nimesh Gopal Pradhan and Dinesh Baniya Kshatri

entry.summary: This paper stores a video and its audio as the weights of a single SIREN network mapping space-time coordinates to RGB and audio, then compresses via knowledge distillation, quantization, and lossless coding. It is an implicit neural representation approach to joint audio-video codecs.

entry.title: Ptolemy's Equant Equates to a Universal Dynamical Clock via Machine Learning

author.name: Jingdong Zhang, Luan Yang, Murilo S. Baptista, Zefeng Zhang, Qunxi Zhu, Wei Lin, and Celso Grebogi

entry.summary: This paper establishes a universal dynamical clock principle in which arbitrary nonlinear oscillations are represented as uniform rotation through an equant-induced nonlinear coordinate, inspired by Ptolemy's equant and Kepler's areal law, using a machine-learning framework. It constructs the equant and phase dynamics for a broad class of oscillatory systems under forcing.

entry.title: Implicit Virtual Leader: Decentralized Vision-Only Relative Pose Estimation for Multi-Robot Formations

author.name: Shiyuan Yang, Zelin Wang, Zhijia Tao, Yilin Wang, Zhengyu Hou, Xiaosong Kong, Borong Zhang, Yip Fun Yeung, Yuankai Luo, Sharon Lee, Qingbiao Li

entry.summary: This work introduces a decentralized, vision-only relative pose estimation framework for multi-robot formations using GNNs and an implicit virtual leader reference frame not tied to any single robot. It adds heteroscedastic and MC-Dropout uncertainty heads and validates across simulation and real hardware.

entry.title: Behavioral Controllability of Agentic Models for Information Extraction: From Fixed Workflows to Reflective Agents

author.name: Lujia Zhang, Xingzhou Chen, Hongwei Feng

entry.summary: This study empirically probes whether agentic components like reflection and memory yield observable, controllable gains over fixed LLM workflows in scholarly dataset extraction from PDFs. It emphasizes process-level metrics such as tool execution, retries, and failure recovery rather than only extraction accuracy.

entry.title: Per-Stroke Temporal Control for Text-to-Motion via Action Units and Action-Detection Guidance

author.name: Euijun Jung, Youngki Lee

entry.summary: The paper introduces Action Units as typed temporal events that make individual motion strokes an explicit conditioning signal for text-to-motion generation, addressing poor per-stroke timing control. It grounds a frozen backbone via a gated adapter and refines timing at inference with a training-free classifier gradient, evaluated on a new StrokeBench.

entry.title: IoUPD: IoU-Aware Privileged Distillation for Visual Grounding with Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Xiuyuan Zhu, Ke Lu, Hao Wu, Zijin Du, Dongming Zhang, Jian Xue

entry.summary: IoUPD is an IoU-aware privileged distillation method for coordinate-generating multimodal LLMs in visual grounding, addressing the mismatch between token-likelihood training and geometric-overlap evaluation. It uses ground-truth boxes as privileged training-time guidance to a frozen teacher.

entry.title: HybridSim: A Physics-Learning Hybrid Digital Twin for mmWave Human Sensing

author.name: Weitao Xiong, Tianyu Liu, Peng Li, Kok Chung Chua, Toa Chean Khim, Pu Wang, and Hongfei Xue

entry.summary: HybridSim is a physics-learning hybrid simulator that synthesizes mmWave radar signals from dynamic human meshes, decoupling propagation into direct paths modeled via inverse rendering with a microfacet BRDF and indirect paths. It reduces the need for expensive site-specific labeled radar data for human sensing.

entry.title: Beyond Frontiers: Scene-Anomaly Guided Autonomous Exploration

author.name: Akash Kumbar, Abhinav Raundhal, Madhava Krishna

entry.summary: SCAGE reframes autonomous 3D exploration as geometric anomaly minimization rather than coverage-maximizing frontier chasing, operating directly on unstructured point clouds with a learned prior over standard indoor architecture. This structural context aims to improve trajectory efficiency and reconstruction fidelity.

entry.title: Dynamics-Aware Meta-Imitation for Generalization to Unseen Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Zhenduo Shang, Xiyao Liu, Bohan Li, Xudong Wang, Teng Ren, Lianqing Liu, Zhi Han

entry.summary: DAMI is a dynamics-aware meta-imitation framework for robotic manipulation that uses meta-learning to build a shared skill space for rapid adaptation to unseen tasks, with a visual-motor trajectory module for spatio-temporal dynamics and an unpaired unified task block to fuse multimodal observations. It targets the generalization gap of imitation learning beyond in-domain tasks.

entry.title: MDND: Unsupervised Learning Guided by Non-Differentiable Refinement for Shape Correspondence

author.name: Qinsong Li and Jing Meng and Haibo Wang and Shengjun Liu

entry.summary: MDND is a deep functional map paradigm for shape correspondence that merges differentiable and non-differentiable components, enabling unsupervised learning guided by an internal non-differentiable multiscale iterative refinement. This overcomes the end-to-end differentiability constraint that caps performance on challenging non-isometric shapes.

entry.title: A Solution to Cryptographic Boxes for Unfriendly AI

author.name: Lysandre Terrisse

entry.summary: Revisits Christiano's 2010 proposal of cryptographic boxes for sandboxing dangerous AI and argues that Secure Multi-Party Computation, rather than homomorphic encryption, provides sandboxing without computational assumptions and much faster. It illustrates the idea by running Game of Life patterns under an MPC protocol.

entry.title: Vision-Language Model Purified Semi-Supervised Semantic Segmentation for Remote Sensing Images

author.name: Shanwen Wang, Xin Sun, Danfeng Hong, Fei Zhou

entry.summary: SemiEarth uses vision-language models to purify noisy pseudo-labels in semi-supervised semantic segmentation for remote sensing, improving teacher-student learning especially at multi-class boundaries. It leverages open-vocabulary VLM knowledge to guide the student model.

entry.title: Stochastic Reset Pathfinding: Path-Level Regret for Cascading Bandits over Graph Paths

author.name: Guni Sharon, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: Stochastic Reset Pathfinding is an episodic bandit problem on a known graph with unknown edge success probabilities where any edge failure resets the agent to the source, making the optimal policy open-loop and placing it in the cascading bandit framework. The authors propose UCB and Thompson Sampling variants of a Log-Dijkstra meta-algorithm with a path-level regret bound.

entry.title: Beyond a Joke: Multi-Angle Reasoning for Detecting and Explaining Harmful Humor in Memes

author.name: Shanhong Liu, Pai Chet Ng, De Wen Soh, Malika Meghjani, Konstantinos N. Plataniotis

entry.summary: MAR-12 is a framework that interprets memes through twelve structured perspectives using vision-language models to detect and explain harmful humor where sarcasm and hateful intent coexist. It aims for reliable classification with human-interpretable structured reasoning.

entry.title: Design-Based Supervised Learning with Noisy Human Labels

author.name: Robert Chew, Matthew R. Williams

entry.summary: PA-DSL is a design-based supervised learning method that corrects noisy human audit labels using adjudicated cases, then debiases analyses over the full set of automated labels while remaining valid for many downstream analyses when audit and adjudication probabilities are known. It addresses realistic settings where human audit labels are imperfect.

entry.title: Inpainting Insights: Elevating Visual XAI with Photorealistic Perturbations

author.name: Josef Lindl, Mariana Chaves, Damien Garreau

entry.summary: This work improves visual explainability by replacing crude pixel perturbations in methods like LIME with photorealistic inpainted perturbations, avoiding unrealistic out-of-distribution samples and visible artifacts that mislead the model. It aims to produce higher-quality, more faithful explanations for image classifiers.

entry.title: Environment Design for Reliable Shared Autonomy with Probabilistic Guarantees

author.name: Yi-Shiuan Tung, Himanshu Gupta, Gyanig Kumar, Heyang Huang, Bradley Hayes, Alessandro Roncone

entry.summary: This work reframes shared autonomy by optimizing workspace design itself to make candidate goals more separable under noisy user inputs, deriving a probabilistic correctness guarantee under bounded noise. Simulations and a real-world system show optimized layouts improve goal inference reliability.

entry.title: Efficient Difficulty-Aware Dynamic Routing for Diffusion-Based Real-World Image Super-Resolution

author.name: Xue Wu, Kang Zhao, Kafeng Wang, Jianfei Chen, Jingwei Xin, Nannan Wang, Xinbo Gao

entry.summary: The paper proposes a difficulty-aware dynamic routing strategy for diffusion-based real-world image super-resolution, allocating processing based on per-image restoration difficulty rather than uniform handling. It also targets detail loss from aggressive VAE downsampling in stable diffusion backbones.

entry.title: Transient State Reorganization and Cell Differentiation in the Developmental Dynamics of Growing Neural Cellular Automata

author.name: Hiroki Sato, Atsushi Masumori, Takashi Ikegami

entry.summary: The paper traces the full developmental trajectory of Growing Neural Cellular Automata, revealing non-monotonic morphological convergence through transient intermediate states and self-organized modular grouping of hidden channels. Geometric analysis shows cell states diversify within a low-dimensional smooth manifold.

entry.title: AuEmoChat: Authentic Emotion Understanding and Rendering for Conversational Speech Synthesis

author.name: Zhenqi Jia, Yuan Zhao, Aruukhan, Rui Liu, Haizhou Li

entry.summary: AuEmoChat is a conversational speech synthesis framework that learns a discrete authentic-emotion token space via finite scalar quantization, moving beyond limited predefined emotion categories. It also addresses redundant multimodal tokens in multi-turn dialogue history for better context understanding.

entry.title: Data-Native Global Optimization for Big Data K-means Clustering

author.name: Ravil Mussabayev, Rustam Mussabayev, Zukhra Yerdaliyeva, Kuldeyev Nursultan

entry.summary: Big-means++ is a scalable global-optimization algorithm for big-data K-means that traverses sample-induced surrogate landscapes rather than optimizing the full-data objective, curating inputs to escape poor local minima. It targets arbitrarily tall data accessed only through finite random samples.

entry.title: CAMMAR: Culture-Aware Matryoshka for Metaphorical Arabic Representations

author.name: Suzan Awinat and Alfonso Ortega del Puente

entry.summary: CAMMAR is a representation-learning framework for Arabic that organizes meaning into nested lexical, cultural, and metaphorical subspaces via a Matryoshka-style staged semantic curriculum, countering the collapse of these into one space. It draws on classical rhetorical theory and yields a training-free geometric metaphoricity measure.

entry.title: Contextual Semantic Relevance Tracks fMRI BOLD Responses During Naturalistic Speech Comprehension

author.name: Kun Sun and Rong Wang

entry.summary: This neuro-NLP study tests whether contextual semantic relevance, capturing how strongly an incoming word relates to recent context, predicts fMRI BOLD responses during naturalistic speech comprehension better than surprisal. It analyzes two public datasets with generalized additive mixed models.

entry.title: How Much Human Label Variation Does Formal Semantic Structure Explain?: Group-Level Effects and Item-Level Ceilings in NLI

author.name: Haram Choi (University of Bremen)

entry.summary: This paper measures how much of human label variation in natural language inference is explained by formal semantic structure, using rule-based operator and monotonicity tagging on over 3,000 ChaosNLI items. It finds group-level effects such as higher entropy for non-upward-monotone hypotheses but item-level ceilings, with full reporting including negative results.

entry.title: Which Hyperparameters Matter? A Game-Theoretic Framework for Interpretable Hyperparameter Sensitivity Analysis

author.name: Nyi Nyi Aung, Heepeom Shin, Abigail Lawlor, Adrian Stein

entry.summary: This work presents a game-theoretic framework for interpretable hyperparameter sensitivity analysis using Shapley Effects for global importance and Pareto fronts to identify effective configurations. Rather than a new optimizer, it reveals which hyperparameters most influence different objectives to guide search and early model evaluation.

entry.title: ContinuityBench: A Benchmark and Systems Study of Stateful Failover in Multi-Provider LLM Routing

author.name: Vishal Pandey, Gopal Singh

entry.summary: ContinuityBench introduces metrics (Continuity Preservation Rate and Continuity Latency Overhead) and a stateful multi-provider proxy architecture with a history-forwarding strategy to preserve conversation state during LLM provider failover. It shows naive stateless failover maintains uptime but silently discards conversation history.

entry.title: HETA++: Global Structure-from-Motion with Hybrid Explicit Translation Averaging

author.name: Peilin Tao, Hainan Cui, Mengqi Rong and Shuhan Shen

entry.summary: HETA++ is a global structure-from-motion framework for translation averaging that hybridly combines relative translations and feature tracks, refining relative translations with global rotations and removing inconsistent ones before convex distance-based position estimation. It aims to be robust under collinear camera motion and outliers.

entry.title: Partial Information Decomposition as a Multi-Contrast 3D MRI Selection Strategy for Resource-Constrained Deep Neural Network Training in Brain Tumor Segmentation

author.name: Agamdeep Chopra, Mehmet Kurt

entry.summary: This paper uses Partial Information Decomposition to rank MRI contrast pairs by redundant, unique, and synergistic information about tumor burden, selecting the best pair to reduce compute in brain tumor segmentation. The selected T1c plus T2-FLAIR pair nearly matches four-input performance with lightweight 3D U-Nets.

entry.title: A Benchmark for Electrical Load Forecasting Across Grid Levels: Time-Series Transformers Outperform Established Methods

author.name: Matthias Hertel, Sebastian P\"utz, Jonathan Kolar, Benjamin Sch\"afer, Ralf Mikut, Veit Hagenmeyer

entry.summary: The authors present a multi-level benchmark for electrical load forecasting spanning transmission control areas, low-voltage feeders, and individual consumers, finding Transformer approaches consistently beat established methods by 6.6 to 10.7 percent. They introduce YAformer, a configurable Transformer to study architectural design choices.

entry.title: CardioMeta: Calibrated Multi-Task Prediction of Diabetes, Hypertension, and Cardiovascular Disease Across Population and EHR Data

author.name: S M Asif Hossain, Ruksat Khan Shayoni, M. F. Mridha, and Jungpil Shin

entry.summary: CardioMeta is a calibrated multi-task framework jointly predicting diabetes, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease across population survey (NHANES) and EHR (MIMIC-IV) data. It emphasizes underreported concerns like label leakage, calibration, temporal robustness, transportability, and subgroup reliability.

entry.title: A Task-Space Receding Horizon Controller for Fast Collision Avoidance

author.name: Mattia Penzotti, Marco Controzzi

entry.summary: This robotics paper presents a task-space receding-horizon controller for fast manipulator collision avoidance that uses a short contact-consistent rollout to build a terminal kinematic reference, then computes only the first control input. It balances the foresight of full MPC with the efficiency of reactive methods.

entry.title: Learning Faster without Deeper Networks: A*-Inspired Batch Selection for Efficient CNN Training

author.name: Anxhelo Shehu, Enes Stastoli and Arben Cela

entry.summary: A*-Inspired Batch Selection reformulates mini-batch scheduling for CNN training as a heuristic search, ranking batches by a loss-based difficulty score combined with a reuse penalty. It is model-agnostic and aims to speed convergence and preserve learning signal without changing architectures.

entry.title: CoG-Guided Weight Correction for Fault-Tolerant Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Bahram Parchekani, Samira Nazari, Ali Azarpeyvand, Mohammad Hasan Ahmadilivani, Tara Ghasempouri, Jaan Raik

entry.summary: This paper proposes a Center of Gravity guided weight correction method that restores faulty DNN weights using distance-aware rules based on their spatial position within a layer, without retraining or architecture changes. It is evaluated via fault injection at varying bit-error rates on safety-critical LSTM networks.

entry.title: Scaling Time Series Classification via XAI-Driven Data Reduction

author.name: Davide Italo Serramazza, Thach Le Nguyen, and Georgiana Ifrim

entry.summary: drXAI repurposes XAI attribution methods for data reduction in time series classification, using a fast GPU-accelerated classifier to generate local attributions aggregated into global feature-importance scores. It addresses the quadratic and linear complexity that makes SOTA Transformer classifiers prohibitive on massive datasets.

entry.title: On the Geometry of Learned Representations in Event-Based Multi-Modal Egomotion Estimation

author.name: Stefano Silvestrini and Michele Ceresoli

entry.summary: This paper analyzes the internal geometry of a multi-modal network fusing event tensors, inertial, and range data for egomotion estimation, showing embeddings lie on low-dimensional motion-aligned manifolds and attention adapts to angular excitation and visual reliability. It offers interpretability of learned representations versus classical geometric optimization.

entry.title: Knowledge-Assisted Multi-Graph Dependency Learning for Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection in Multi-Stage Industrial Processes

author.name: Jaeyeong Lee, Taeseong Yoon, Wonmo Koo, Heeyoung Kim

entry.summary: This work proposes a knowledge-assisted multi-graph dependency learning method for multivariate time-series anomaly detection in multi-stage industrial processes, incorporating process knowledge that GNN-based methods typically overlook. It models complex dependencies across variables and process stages.

entry.title: Conditional Reliability of Toxicity Signals for Multilingual and Code-Mixed Abuse Detection

author.name: Indraveni Chebolu, Rohan Singh, Arnab Mallick, Harmesh Rana

entry.summary: ToxGate is a trust-fusion head that conditions each auxiliary toxicity signal on the encoder representation before adding it to the prediction, studying the conditional reliability of toxicity priors for Indian multilingual and code-mixed abuse detection. It improves over plain encoders in most in-domain and transfer settings.

entry.title: Minimum Time Dubins Airplane Paths with Asymmetric Climb Rates

author.name: Jaeyoung Lim, Giuseppe Loianno

entry.summary: This paper extends Dubins airplane paths to asymmetric climb and descent rate constraints for fixed-wing vehicles, revisiting time-optimality conditions to show asymmetric flight-path-angle constraints preserve optimality. Exploiting full vehicle performance reduces minimum connection time by up to 71 percent.

entry.title: Domain Knowledge-Enhanced LLMs for Fraud and Concept Drift Detection

author.name: Ali \c{S}enol, Garima Agrawal, Huan Liu

entry.summary: The authors propose a domain-knowledge-enhanced LLM framework that injects structured task-specific insights to detect fraud and concept drift in evolving conversations. It targets the problem of shifting language patterns that obscure malicious intent.

entry.title: How Does Empowering Users with Greater System Control Affect News Filter Bubbles?

author.name: Ping Liu, Karthik Shivaram, Aron Culotta, Matthew Shapiro, Mustafa Bilgic

entry.summary: This study builds a political news recommender with a transparent interface exposing inferred political and topical interests and letting users adjust their feed, then runs a user study on filter bubbles. It finds transparency and control help users diversify exposure.

entry.title: Position: Quantum Program Generation Must Prioritize Validity Over Probabilistic Scaling

author.name: Junhao Song, Yu Zhou, William Knottenbelt, Yudong Cao

entry.summary: This position paper argues that applying the parameter-scaling paradigm to quantum circuit generation is a directional error because valid circuits require strict mathematical constraints and the valid subset shrinks exponentially with qubits. It advocates a shift from human copilots to verifier-centric agents with hierarchical constraints and topological masks.

entry.title: Explicit Over Implicit: Enhancing CNNs Via Complex Structure Tensor Representations for Periocular Recognition

author.name: Kevin Hernandez-Diaz, Josef Bigun, Fernando Alonso-Fernandez

entry.summary: This study shows that feeding the Complex Structure Tensor, which encodes compact orientation features with certainties, into CNNs improves periocular recognition over grayscale inputs and lets smaller networks beat larger ones. It argues CNNs struggle to extract orientation features and that explicit orientation input mitigates this.

entry.title: qZACH-ViT: Quantization-Aware Intrinsic Explanations with Recursive Attribution-Stabilized Optimization

author.name: Athanasios Angelakis

entry.summary: qZACH-ViT is a quantization-aware, CLS-token-free vision transformer with recursive patch-level class evidence and a Recursive Attribution-Stabilized Optimization method that aligns classification and attribution gradients. It targets efficient, interpretable medical image classifiers deployed as INT8 ONNX graphs.

entry.title: Deployment-Ready UWB Localization for Industrial Ground Robots with Automatic Anchor Calibration and Terrain-Aware Fusion

author.name: Alexander Raab, Giulio Delama, Roland Jung, Stephan Weiss

entry.summary: This paper presents a deployment-ready UWB localization pipeline for industrial ground robots combining automatic static-anchor calibration with a terrain-aware multi-sensor estimator tailored to surface-bound motion. It reduces the time-consuming, error-prone anchor setup that limits real-world AMR deployments.

entry.title: DECODEM: Data Extraction from Corporate Organizational Documents via Enhanced Methods

author.name: Jens Frankenreiter

entry.summary: DECODEM provides benchmark datasets pairing randomly sampled corporate charters and bylaws with high-quality human annotations of governance provisions, for evaluating automated extraction of structured variables. It compares LLM extraction pipelines varying in prompt design and task decomposition.

entry.title: Enhancing Hepatopathy Clinical Trial Efficiency: A Secure, Large Language Model-Powered Pre-Screening Pipeline

author.name: Xiongbin Gui, Hanlin Lv, Xiao Wang, Longting Lv, Yi Xiao and Lei Wang

entry.summary: This paper builds a privacy-conscious LLM pipeline that decomposes complex liver-disease trial eligibility criteria into composite questions and answers them over electronic health records. It is a domain application aimed at speeding clinical trial pre-screening while addressing accuracy and privacy concerns.

entry.title: A Physics-Informed Neural Network with a Modified Lorentzian Activation for Nonlocal Gradient-Flow Equations in Dynamic Density Functional Theory

author.name: Dimitrios Gourzoulidis, Soumaya Elkantassi, Serafim Kalliadasis

entry.summary: The paper develops a physics-informed neural network for nonlocal gradient-flow equations in dynamic density functional theory, adding a modified Lorentzian activation and a precomputed discrete operator for the nonlocal convolution. It targets slow convergence and hard optimization in standard PINNs.

entry.title: Lazy Arithmetic using Systolic Arrays for Closing the Verification Gap on Embedded Systems

author.name: Taisa Kushner (Galois Inc), Ryan McCleeary (Galois Inc), Martin Brain (City St George University of London)

entry.summary: This paper proposes a lazy-arithmetic approach on systolic arrays to close the verification gap for deploying deep neural networks on safety-critical embedded systems resistant to fault injection. It seeks correctness-oriented, sound, and optimal edge inference where existing quantization schemes fall short.

entry.title: Proactive Inpatient Bed Requests for Emergency Department Admissions

author.name: QIan Cheng, Nilay Tanik Argon, Aniruddhan Ganesaraman, Serhan Ziya

entry.summary: This work formulates proactive inpatient bed requests for emergency department admissions as a Markov decision process, aggregating admission-probability and time-to-disposition predictions to request beds early. It derives three data-driven policies via approximate dynamic programming, reinforcement learning, and a newsvendor approach, evaluated in simulation.

entry.title: The Third Competition on Document Forgery Detection on ID-Cards and Passports

author.name: Juan E. Tapia, Mario Nieto, Juan M. Espin, \'Alvaro S. Rocamora, Javier Barrachina, Naser Damer, Christoph Busch

entry.summary: This report analyzes the Third International Competition on Document Forgery Detection for ID cards and passports across a synthetic-data track and a heterogeneous cross-domain attack track. The Incode team won both, with results underscoring the need for balanced, generalizable presentation-attack detection.

entry.title: Agentic Synthesis against Counterexample-Supplemented Sketches

author.name: Muness Castle, Eric Rubeck

entry.summary: This paper introduces agentic synthesis against counterexample-supplemented sketches, a repository-native method where a human provides a partial code sketch and a coding agent iteratively revises it as concrete failures expose missing domain policy. It preserves provenance and gates revisions with a regression set to prevent repeating plausible mistakes.

entry.title: A Semiparametric Framework for Stochastic Fundamental Diagram Modeling

author.name: Pengnan Chi, Xiaoliang Ma, Magnus Jansson, Magnus Nordenvaad

entry.summary: This paper proposes a semiparametric framework for stochastic fundamental diagram modeling in traffic, using specially designed functional forms that intrinsically satisfy physical moment constraints while embedding neural structures for complex nonlinear patterns. It derives moment-matching equations to enforce physical constraints on conditional flow distributions.

entry.title: On the Failure of Boundary-Seeking Distillation in Bottlenecked Generative Architectures

author.name: Mohamed Amine Kina

entry.summary: This paper shows that boundary-seeking data-free knowledge distillation, effective for classifiers, fundamentally fails in bottlenecked generative architectures like autoencoders. Reformulating reconstruction as per-feature classification on MNIST, it argues instance-level boundary objectives are ill-posed for decoders with many coupled outputs.

entry.title: Structure of the Circular-Dyadic Convolution Error

author.name: Ben Fauber and Alireza Moradzadeh

entry.summary: This theoretical work characterizes the error introduced when substituting the Hadamard transform for the DFT in dyadic versus circular convolution, identifying exact error-free positions, near-full-rank error structure, and a closed-form expected-error scalar. It clarifies the algebraic cost of the faster real-valued transform.

entry.title: Unsupervised Keypoints for Real-Time Fall Detection: Comparative Analysis Under Real-world Conditions with Predictive Bandwidth Reduction

author.name: Tasmiah Haque, Jacob Kosinski, Sumit Mohan, Srinjoy Das, Mohammad Abdullah Al-Mamun

entry.summary: This work proposes a privacy-preserving real-time fall detection framework that replaces RGB transmission with compact unsupervised keypoints and predictive temporal modeling, using variational recurrent prediction plus sequence classification. It is evaluated on fall datasets under realistic conditions with bandwidth reduction.

entry.title: Closed-Loop Bayesian Bandit Encoder with GRAND Receiver for a Bursty Interference Channel

author.name: Bhaskar Krishnamachari

entry.summary: This single-author paper combines a Bayesian bandit encoder that selects between a random linear code and an interleaved version with a GRAND receiver using a hidden-Markov noise model, over a bursty interference channel with unknown interferers. Aggregate channel statistics are fed back to guide transmission mode selection.

entry.title: AI Trading: Evaluating Large Language Models for Technical Market Analysis

author.name: Geofrey Ntale

entry.summary: This paper systematically evaluates five LLMs including GPT-4 Turbo, Claude 3 Opus, and Gemini 1.5 Pro plus domain-specialized FinGPT on technical market analysis tasks like candlestick recognition, signal generation, backtesting, and report comprehension. It uses financial and NLP metrics across the pipeline.

entry.title: Personalized Image Aesthetic Assessment via Preference-rich Sample Mining and Cohort Merging

author.name: Zhichao Yang, Tianjiao Gu, Zhixianhe Zhang, Xiangfei Sheng, Pengfei Chen, Leida Li

entry.summary: PRAC is a multimodal-LLM approach to personalized image aesthetic assessment that mines preference-rich samples via collective controversy and personalized deviation, then merges aesthetically resonant user cohorts. It aims to model individual aesthetic preferences from limited per-user data.

entry.title: AgentFAIR: A Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework for FAIRness Evaluation of Geospatial Datasets

author.name: Ming Chen, Pranav Pai

entry.summary: AgentFAIR is a multi-agent framework combining structured metadata extraction with 13 sub-principle-specific LLM evaluators to assess FAIR compliance of geospatial datasets. The authors show existing FAIR tools disagree substantially, motivating a more consistent LLM-based approach.

entry.title: Cost-efficient generative AI summarization for scalable automated essay scoring in educational assessment

author.name: Haowei Hua

entry.summary: This study proposes a generative-AI summarization framework for scalable automated essay scoring, generating controlled-length summaries with three existing GPT-5 variants and combining them with handcrafted linguistic features in a hybrid model. It aims to overcome transformer input-length limits for long essays while controlling cost.

entry.title: Perceived AGI: Believability as Dimensional Completeness, Not Capability

author.name: Sebastian Cochinescu

entry.summary: This position-style HCI paper argues that the believability of an AI interlocutor depends on dimensional completeness across four first-person stances (time, truth, entropy, and love) rather than more task capability. It frames perceived mind as separable from task intelligence and offers concrete emulation paths.

entry.title: Hardware-triggered Time Synchronization of Roadside Multi-lidar, Multi-camera Measurement System for Accurate Data Alignment

author.name: Shiva Agrawal, Savankumar Bhanderi, Zhiran Yan, and Gordon Elger
